evidence.text: NSSF-adjusted NICS background checks for the three calendar months that are SPWH's fiscal Q2 (quarter ends 1 Aug 2026) ran May +3.2% (1,105,758), June +11.7% (1,123,006) and July +8.5% (1,061,883) YoY -- roughly +7.7% for the quarter -- versus only +3.5% (Feb) and +1.9% (Mar) in the fiscal Q1 in which SPWH delivered +2.1% same-store sales and +6.3% hunting/shooting; the two strongest months were published on 6 July and 5 August, after management reaffirmed FY comps of -1.0% to +2.0% on 2 June with visibility only through soft May.
evidence.source_date: 2026-07-06 (publication date stated on page; URL path /2026/07/)
evidence.why_not_priced: A 30 Aug 2026 preview states the market expects SPWH revenue 'flat year on year' and that analysts have 'generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days' -- i.e. the three estimates did not move after the 6 July (+11.7%) and 5 August (+8.5%) NICS releases (https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/sportsmans-warehouse-earnings-look-spwh-030052393.html, dated 2026-08-30 in the document). If it were priced the estimate revision breadth would be positive, the FY comp guide would already be treated as stale, and the stock would not be sitting 5.8% above its 52-week low with a +3.0% 20-day run-up a month after Ruger disclosed +19% retail sell-through. On top of that, no US outdoor peer has yet reported this window: Academy does not report fiscal Q2 until 9 September 2026 (https://investors.academy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/academy-sports-outdoors-announces-second-quarter-fiscal-2026), so SPWH prints first and there is no peer datapoint in the tape.
evidence.independence: Two different source classes point the same way and neither is a background-check statistic. (1) Sturm Ruger, 29 July 2026: net sales +19%, estimated sell-through from distributors to retailers +19% versus 'a 5% increase in adjusted NICS', with distributor inventories DOWN 45,800 units and factory finished goods down 100,100 units -- that is SPWH's own inbound channel destocking on retail pull-through (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729922943/en/Sturm-Ruger-Company-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results, date in URL path 20260729). (2) Olin's Winchester segment Q2 2026: sales +11.8% to $500.3m on higher commercial ammunition volume AND price, with tariffs reducing import competition, and management guiding to sequential improvement into the fall hunting season (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/olin-oln-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/, date in URL path 2026/08/07). NOTE ON OVERLAP: these are corroboration for this one finding, not separate findings -- they measure the same underlying demand acceleration and are folded into this single +5.0, deliberately not counted twice.

evidence.text: The $200 NFA transfer tax on suppressors fell to $0 on 1 January 2026, and NFA background checks have roughly doubled-to-tripled in SPWH's fiscal Q2 window (May 2026 146,551 vs 73,138, +100.4%; June 2026 166,677 vs 60,147, +177.1%; July 2026 130,013, +108.8%) -- and SPWH has been selling suppressors online through a 'Delivered by Silencer Central' drop-ship partnership since 12 March 2025, yet the words suppressor, silencer and NFA do not appear anywhere on its Q1 2026 earnings call.
evidence.source_date: 2025-03-12 (date in URL path /2025/03/12/ -- deliberately checked, this is a 2025 release and predates the tax change)
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no sell-side model line for this: the category is not in SPWH's reported department disclosure, was never quantified on a call, and is not mentioned in the 30 Aug preview. If it were priced, at least one of the three estimates would have been raised off it, and the 'weak outdoor retail' framing in the wire copy would instead read as a new-category story. The check on whether the category is worth anything at retail is not SPWH's own words but Academy's: on its 10 June 2026 call Academy said suppressors were launched in a limited number of stores, are going to 100+ stores by year-end, and are '100% accretive as it is entirely new to the assortment, benefiting from recent changes in procurement laws'.
evidence.independence: Academy Sports and Outdoors' Q1 2026 call on 10 June 2026 independently validates the category economics and the causal link to the law change: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/academy-sports-outdoors-inc-q1-123000366.html (article date 2026-06-10, stated in the document). The NFA check counts come from a different source again: https://www.ammoland.com/2026/08/july-2026-gun-sales-nics-nfa-checks-surge/ (date in URL path /2026/08/) and https://www.ammoland.com/2026/07/june-2026-nics-nfa-suppressor-checks-surge/ (/2026/07/). This is a distinct fact from finding 1 -- a statutory change and a new category, not a comp rate -- but I note the NFA check series and the NICS series are published by the same body, so a scorer collapsing NSSF releases into one cluster should treat this finding's residual as the Silencer Central channel and the Academy read, not the check counts.

evidence.text: The 8-K filed 24 June 2026 (event 18 June 2026) pushed BOTH the senior secured revolver (resized $350m to $315m) and the $45m ABL term loan out to 18 June 2031, removing the 27 May 2027 revolver maturity that was still disclosed in the Q1 10-Q alongside $114.6m of borrowing-base availability -- so the balance-sheet mechanism that produced this stock's two extreme prints (-29.8% on 4 Dec 2025, +97.9% on 1 Apr 2025) cannot recur in the same form at this print.
evidence.why_not_priced: The fact is public and ten weeks old, so I am NOT claiming the extension itself is unpriced -- I am claiming its effect on the shape of this reaction is. The sealed baseline's 14.1% expected move is the median of eight prints, two of which (-29.8%, +97.9%) were refinancing/liquidity events under a facility that matured inside two years; with no maturity inside five years and $114.6m of availability, that left tail is structurally smaller here and the baseline number is mechanically too wide. If the market had re-underwritten the equity for a five-year runway the stock would not still be trading at $1.185 with a $45m market cap and a +3.0% 20-day run-up, i.e. still priced as a distressed option; that non-reaction is the observable evidence. The signed impact is small on purpose -- the content is a narrower distribution, not a direction.
evidence.independence: The old 27 May 2027 maturity and the $114.6m availability come from the Q1 10-Q, a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001132105/000119312526253546/spwh-20260502.htm (period ended 2026-05-02, filed June 2026). The resizing rationale ('to better align the facility's size with current operating needs') is separately reported at https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:6792bc30e6cb1:0-sportsman-s-warehouse-refinances-abl-term-loan-to-2031-amends-revolver-with-wells-fargo/. I also confirmed from EDGAR that this is the ONLY 8-K SPWH has filed since 1 June 2026 -- no Nasdaq notice, no impairment, no pre-announcement.

evidence.text: The demand that is accelerating is SPWH's lowest-margin demand: Q1 2026 gross margin fell to 29.6% from 30.4% specifically because firearms and ammunition mix rose while higher-margin categories declined, Q1 adjusted EBITDA was -$8.1m against a full-year guide of $30-36m that is therefore entirely back-half-loaded, and Academy told investors on 10 June 2026 -- eight days after SPWH last spoke -- that it was 'tracking at flat comparable sales through the Memorial Day period' on 'persistent $4+ gas prices'.
evidence.source_date: 2026-06-02 (Q1 FY2026 press release, thirteen weeks ended 2026-05-02, filed as 8-K Ex-99)
evidence.why_not_priced: The gross margin mechanic is disclosed, so what is unpriced is its interaction with finding 1, not the fact itself: a NICS-led revenue beat can arrive with a lower gross margin rate and, with ~$148.4m of net debt carrying interest, still miss on EPS. If the market had worked this through, the coverage would frame a firearms-led beat as margin-dilutive rather than as good news, and the 30 Aug preview would not simply say 'revenue flat'. Academy's flat-through-Memorial-Day comment is the reason I do not extrapolate the whole +7.7% NICS quarter into comps -- the non-firearm half of the box (camp, apparel, footwear) is still fighting $4 gasoline.
evidence.independence: The Academy datapoint is from a genuinely different entity and postdates SPWH's last public statement: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/academy-sports-outdoors-inc-q1-123000366.html (2026-06-10). SPWH's own Q1 language on 'continued consumer economic pressure and higher fuel prices' points the same way from the company's own release. OVERLAP DISCLOSED: this finding and finding 1 read the SAME underlying fact -- firearms/ammunition-led growth -- on opposite lines of the P&L (revenue vs gross margin rate). It is filed as a signed offset, not as independent negative evidence, and finding 1's +5.0 is already net of a gross-margin haircut; the two together are one thesis with an honest downside vent, not two theses. Finding 4 also shares the Q1 press release with the guidance and EBITDA figures cited in finding 1's supporting URLs.

NSSF-adjusted NICS for SPWH's exact fiscal Q2 window (May 1,105,758 / June 1,123,006 / July 1,061,883 = 3,290,647 vs 3,055,402 a year earlier, +7.7%) accelerated 5.4 points from the ~+2.3% of its fiscal Q1 (Feb +3.5%, Mar +1.9%, Apr +1.6%), the quarter in which SPWH printed +2.1% comps and +7.4% hunting-and-shooting.
evidence.why_not_priced: The July NICS release (5 Aug), Ruger's Q2 call (7 Aug) and Olin's Q2 release (30 Jul) all landed inside the baseline's 20-day window, and the baseline's 20-day run-up is +3.04% of which +3.95% is the last five days alone - i.e. the tape was flat or down through the exact days the sector data printed, and the small gain is pre-earnings drift. If this were priced, the 3-estimate consensus would sit above the company's reaffirmed -1%/+2% comp guide instead of at ($0.11) vs ($0.12) a year ago (no YoY improvement), and a $45m equity levered on $148.4m of net debt would not have absorbed a 5-point acceleration in its primary demand driver for a 3% drift. There is no transmission mechanism: ~276k shares/day (~$330k notional), 3 estimates, 23 contracts of total option open interest.
evidence.independence: Two supply-side sources, neither derived from NICS: Sturm Ruger's Q2 2026 release (29 Jul 2026) reports estimated sell-through from distributors to retailers +19% YoY with distributor inventories DOWN 45,800 units and finished-goods down 100,100 units - https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729922943/en/Sturm-Ruger-Company-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results ; and Olin's Q2 2026 release (30 Jul 2026) shows Winchester sales $500.3m vs $447.6m (+11.8%) with segment earnings up on 'higher commercial ammunition pricing AND volume' - https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/olin-announces-second-quarter-2026-results-302839441.html . Caveat I could not close: NFA (suppressor) checks are up 108.8% in July and 177% in June after the $200 transfer tax was removed, and I could not verify from NSSF methodology whether NFA sits inside the adjusted series, so some of the +7.7% may be a category SPWH monetises only as a drop-ship referral. Ruger's unit sell-through and Winchester's ammo volume are NFA-independent and are why I still size this positive.

evidence.text: This quarter laps the highest gross margin SPWH has posted in the recent run - 32.0% in Q2 FY2025 - while the Q1 FY2026 it just reported came in at 29.6% (down 80bps YoY) with management attributing the contraction specifically to mix into lower-margin firearms and ammunition, which is precisely the category the NICS acceleration drives.
evidence.why_not_priced: The market has the 32.0% number, but the reaction function is the unpriced part: on 2 June 2026 SPWH beat with +2.1% comps and +2.8% sales and the stock moved +2.11%, because gross margin fell 80bps on exactly this mix. So a top-line-only beat is worth roughly nothing on this name, and the difference between a +4% print and a +12% print is entirely whether the 32.0% lap is held and the $30-36m FY EBITDA guide is raised. If the market had focused on this, the 5-day drift would not be positive into a quarter whose margin comparison is its hardest of the year. This is the reason my net number is +4.0 rather than +6.0.
evidence.independence: Shares one document with finding 1 - the Q1 FY2026 earnings release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001132105/000119312526253505/spwh-ex99_pr120722.htm, 2026-06-02) supplies both the +7.4% hunting/shooting comp used above and the 29.6%/-80bps mix explanation used here; treat the two as one source cluster. The independent leg here is the Q2 FY2025 release's 32.0% gross margin (URL above) and the reaffirmed FY2026 guide of -1%/+2% comps and $30-36m adjusted EBITDA against FY2025 actual adjusted EBITDA of $27.5m - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1132105/000119312526134574/spwh-ex99_pr120722.htm (2026-03-31).

evidence.text: The 8-K filed 24 June 2026 amended and restated both facilities out to 18 June 2031 - the $45m ABL term loan and a revolver cut from $350m to $315m - so the near-term maturity wall the price appears to embed is gone, and Q1 liquidity was $116.7m against a minimum-availability covenant of the greater of $30m or 10% of the gross borrowing base.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the one place where I think the baseline's forward distribution is wrong rather than the mean: the -29.8% print of 2025-12-04 that anchors the 14.1% median reaction was a distress-tail event on a company with a live maturity and covenant question, and that mechanism is now five years out with $116.7m of headroom. The stock is still within 5.8% of its 52-week low and did not re-rate on the amendment - a 3% stub of enterprise value should move multiples of the observed 3.04% drift if a five-year term-out were being capitalised. I size it at only +1.0 because the refinancing did get wire coverage (TipRanks, TradingView, Globe and Mail) in late June, so this is a statement about the left tail of this print, not about its mean.
evidence.independence: Confirmed independently by the Q1 FY2026 10-Q's credit-facility note, which states the $45m term loan carried at $44,323k and the minimum-availability covenant of the greater of $30,000k and 10% of the gross borrowing base - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001132105/000119312526253546/spwh-20260502.htm (2026-06-02). Separate wire confirmation of the extension: https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/sportsmans-warehouse-extends-and-restructures-key-credit-facilities

evidence.text: Nasdaq minimum-bid-price / delisting angle from the sweep note: closed as a non-issue. No 8-K disclosing any Nasdaq correspondence, the baseline's 52w low implies the stock has never traded below $1 (spot $1.185, only 5.8% above the low), and on >$1.2bn of revenue SPWH clears the Nasdaq Global Market total-assets/total-revenue continued-listing standard regardless of a $45m market cap. https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001132105&type=8-K
No 8-K of any kind since 2026-06-24 (items 1.01/2.03/9.01, the refinancing). No pre-announcement, no covenant amendment, no management change, no impairment notice in the 10 weeks before the print.

Insider activity: exactly one Form 4 since 5 June - 2026-08-20, CFO Jennifer Fall Jung, 20,580 shares at $1.16, transaction code F (shares withheld for RSU vesting tax). No open-market purchase or sale, no cluster. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001132105/000178454026000006/form4-08202026_040801.xml
Short interest 1.23m shares, 3.41% of float, 2.6 days to cover - no squeeze or crowded-short mechanics to amplify a surprise. https://fintel.io/ss/us/spwh

A story served by search as current, headlined 'Sportsman's Warehouse Closing 23 Doors, Selling 15 Others' with ~2,600 employees affected, is dated 16 March 2009 and describes a 67-store company. Discarded. https://sgbonline.com/sportsmans-warehouse-closing-23-doors-selling-15-others/

Job-board postings (11 US openings on Glassdoor, seasonal hunting-buyer roles open to 30 Sep 2026) could not be date-anchored against any prior count, so no signal either way. https://www.glassdoor.com/Jobs/Sportsman-s-Warehouse-Jobs-E38562.htm

Could not quantify the suppressor/NFA tailwind: SPWH has sold suppressors online with Silencer Central fulfilment since 12 March 2025 (https://www.silencercentral.com/blog/sportsman-warehouse-suppressor-sales/) and NFA checks are up 108-177% YoY, but no SPWH disclosure sizes the channel and the economics are drop-ship, so I left it out of the findings rather than guess.

Company store locator (sportsmans.com/stores) and Fast Company both returned HTTP 403 - could not independently verify current store count or the status of the ~5 underperforming closures management said would happen after the holiday season.

No peer print lands before SPWH on the same May-July quarter: Smith & Wesson reports fiscal Q1 (quarter ended 31 July 2026) only on 3 September 2026, i.e. two days after. https://ir.smith-wesson.com/news-releases/news-release-details/smith-wesson-brands-inc-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial

No tariff commentary at all in the 2 June 2026 Q1 call transcript, and no quarter-to-date comp disclosure beyond a qualitative remark that June would be one of the largest months on Father's Day demand - so no company-sourced Q2 number exists to anchor against.
The 27 May 2026 8-K (items 5.02/5.07) is only an equity-plan amendment and routine annual-meeting results - no reverse split proposal, no share authorisation increase, no executive departure.

evidence.text: CXM's own five prior prints moved +5.96%, -10.00%, +3.05%, +6.05%, -3.03% (close before to close of the print day, all pre-open releases) and the sign is conditioned on the run-in: the only double-digit decline, 2025-09-03, was the print it entered at $8.60 near its 52-week high, which is the same setup as today at $7.94-8.21 after +22.6% in 20 days.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sealed baseline records history.n = 0 and options total open interest of 413 contracts with an ATM bid-ask 143% of mid, i.e. there is literally no market-visible statement of an expected move on this name and nobody is positioned for one. If this conditional base rate were in the price, a 62.7% ATM vol name two sessions from a print would have a two-sided chain and bid puts; instead the only thing in the price is a 20-day run-up that the IGV melt-up explains on its own. The baseline generator itself discarded all 21 prints on CIK 0001569345 as belonging to a predecessor entity, so the reaction history is not even available to whoever built the calendar row.
evidence.independence: Print dates independently confirmed from EDGAR 8-K item 2.02 filings (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001569345.json — 8-Ks of 2025-06-04, 2025-12-03, 2026-03-11, 2026-06-03 and 2025-09-03), so the price windows are anchored to filings rather than to an aggregator. The 2026-06-03 -3.0% is corroborated by ChartMill's 'Falls on Soft Guidance Despite Q1 Beat' (-3.8% cited): https://www.chartmill.com/news/CXM/Chartmill-49384-Sprinklr-NYSECXM-Falls-on-Soft-Guidance-Despite-Q1-Beat

evidence.text: Sprinklr's FY27 non-GAAP operating income guide of $139-141m requires H2 operating income of ~$77-79m against H1 of ~$61.7m (Q1 actual $31.7m plus Q2 guide midpoint $30.0m) — a ~30% step-up in the quarterly run-rate that the CFO justified only as 'improve gradually in the second half of the year as we expect some efficiency gains' — and that FY OI guide had already been cut from $144-146m at the March print.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is guidance arithmetic across two press releases and a transcript, and only 8 analysts cover the name — stockanalysis.com records that their price targets were last updated 2026-06-04, when CXM closed at $5.38, with one refresh since. If the H2 bar were in the price, the average target would not still sit at $7.88 below a $7.99 spot with the stock at a 12-month high; the sell-side has simply not re-underwritten the FY27 OI ramp since the guide was cut, so a second cut lands into unrevised models rather than into pre-positioned ones.
evidence.independence: The March FY27 OI guide of $144-146m that was subsequently cut is in a different document: https://investors.sprinklr.com/news/press-releases/detail/249/sprinklr-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2026 (2026-03-11). The CFO's H2 language is from the Q1 FY27 call transcript, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/04/sprinklr-cxm-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/ — same source cluster as finding 3 below, which I flag there.

evidence.text: The Q2 FY27 revenue guide implies professional services of only ~$20.5m (total $214-215m less subscription $193.5-194.5m) versus actual PS of $24.7m, $27.2m and $28.8m in the last three quarters, and Sprinklr beat its own implied PS guide by 25% in Q3 FY26 ($28.8m actual vs $23.0m implied) and 10% in Q1 FY27 ($24.7m vs $22.5m implied) — so a headline revenue beat of roughly 1.5-2.5% is mechanically likely, but at the -10% PS gross margin management guided it adds nothing to operating income.
evidence.why_not_priced: The wire carries 'Sprinklr poised to beat earnings estimates again' as an undifferentiated positive; what it does not carry is that the beat is structurally located in the one revenue line that runs a negative gross margin, so the headline and the margin move in opposite directions. If this were priced, the sell-side would model PS separately and the stock would not react to the total-revenue line — yet the 2026-06-03 print beat revenue, EPS and operating income and still closed down 3%, which is exactly what a market reading the total line and then the guide does.
evidence.independence: Shares the Q1 FY27 transcript with finding 2, so treat as one source cluster on the guidance-quality point; the PS actuals are from three separate press releases (Q3 FY26 https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251203552368/en/Sprinklr-Announces-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2026-Results, Q4 FY26 https://investors.sprinklr.com/news/press-releases/detail/249/sprinklr-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2026, Q1 FY27 https://www.sprinklr.com/newsroom/sprinklr-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-results/).

evidence.text: In the Q1 FY27 10-Q geographic disaggregation, Americas revenue FELL to $112.9m from $117.6m (-4.0% YoY) while 'Other' jumped to $29.6m from $15.9m (+86%), so 48.6% of revenue is now outside the Americas versus 42.8% a year earlier and 44% for FY26 — Sprinklr's home market is contracting and every dollar of growth is coming from the regions where the Middle East disruption and FX sit.
evidence.why_not_priced: This table is in a 6MB 10-Q note; it is not in the earnings press release, it was not raised on the Q1 call, and no wire copy on the name mentions it. If the market had focused on a declining US base at ~51% of revenue, the story on the tape would be 'domestic decline offset by emerging-market wins', not 'AI transformation and improving renewals' — and a stock whose largest region shrinks does not close at a 12-month high on a 22.6% 20-day run without one analyst refreshing a target since 2026-06-04.
evidence.independence: The 10-K's own statement that 'during the years ended January 31, 2026 and 2025, we generated 44% and 41%, respectively, of our revenue outside the Americas' independently establishes the mix shift trend from a different filing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1569345/000156934526000015/cxm-20260131.htm. Caveat I cannot fully exclude: a segment reclassification between EMEA and Other, though comparatives in the same table should be restated on a like-for-like basis.

evidence.text: The Q1 FY27 10-Q discloses that 'our operations in the Middle East have been affected by the 2026 Iran conflict, including disruptions to our business activities in the region and inaccessibility, and potential loss, of certain customer data in connection with a third-party data center infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates' and warns of 'significant and unanticipated expenses... emergency data transfers, temporary changes to data processing locations, increased infrastructure costs' — and the conflict's targeting of Gulf data centres was still live in July 2026, i.e. across the whole of the quarter being reported (1 May - 31 July 2026).
evidence.why_not_priced: Management framed this on the Q1 call as a discrete quarter event — 54 customers 'moved on the fly' out of a damaged Middle East environment to Ireland and '$3 million to $4 million of slip deals' — and the market treated it as behind them: CXM bottomed at $4.91 on 2026-06-25 and then rose 67% with no company news. If the market had carried it forward into Q2 it would not have re-rated the stock 67% while the same conflict was still striking Gulf data centres in July, and the unquantified infrastructure and remediation costs would show up in sell-side gross-margin estimates that have not been revised since 2026-06-04.
evidence.independence: RBC Capital Markets, 2026-07 (year confirmed in the URL path /2026/07/): https://www.rbccm.com/en/insights/2026/07/data-centers-become-the-new-battleground-in-iran-war establishes the data-centre campaign persisted into the quarter being reported. Origin of the outage independently dated 2026-03-03 by CNBC (year in URL path): https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/03/iran-war-uae-drone-strikes-aws-data-centers.html

evidence.text: The scheduled termination date of Sprinklr's $125m variable-tenor accelerated share repurchase with Citibank is September 1, 2026 — today, the session before the print — after which the dealer's covering purchases (roughly $125m spread over ~115 sessions on a 2.76m-share ADV) stop, and only $75m of the $200m authorization remains through 15 March 2027.
evidence.why_not_priced: The termination date exists only in a 10-Q footnote: on the Q1 call management said only 'we repurchased 17.1 million shares' and '$75 million remaining', with no mention of the September 1 date or the pending final settlement, and no wire copy on the name mentions it. The baseline itself concedes that with no usable option chain 'what is priced' is INFERRED FROM THE RUN-UP — so a mechanical, price-insensitive buyer inside that run-up is precisely the contamination the baseline cannot see. If the market knew the bid ended today, the last four sessions would not have printed 3.2m/4.7m/4.2m/4.6m shares against a 1.7-2.4m ADV three weeks earlier on zero company news. The upper end of my band is real: with $502.5m of cash and $141.9m of FY26 free cash flow, a fresh or expanded authorisation announced with the print is the natural offset.
evidence.independence: The ASR's initial delivery is visible in the tape itself and not just the footnote: on 2026-03-16, the date the 10-Q says Sprinklr paid Citibank and received 17,123,288 shares, CXM traded 18,312,900 shares against a 1.7-2.6m-share ADV in the surrounding sessions (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CXM?period1=1772755200&period2=1773705600&interval=1d). As of April 30, 2026, the ASR Agreement remained unsettled') and appears in no wire story, no preview and no analyst note; if the market had priced the withdrawal of the bid you would not see a 9-analyst average target of $7.88 sitting BELOW a $8.00 spot with nobody having refreshed since June, and you would not see the run-up delivered as a gapless daily grind - a fundamental re-rating on the Ribas board seat (17 Aug) or the Summer '26 release (15 Jul) would have produced a step, and in any case the run began on 1 July, weeks before both.

evidence.text: The quarter being reported (1 May - 31 July 2026) was run without a Chief Revenue Officer for two of its three months: Scott Millard resigned effective 2025-11-11 after roughly seven weeks in the job, Tom Addis did not start until 2026-07-01, and SVP Global Sales Kevin Connolly left for NewRocket in the same window - so tomorrow's Q3 guide is the first ever set by a revenue chief with two months of tenure.

If the market had priced an eight-month CRO vacancy across the seasonally-important Q2 you would expect the stock to be discounting the guide rather than trading 7.5% off its 52-week high with only three EPS estimates and a Hold consensus; a stock that had priced sales-execution risk does not add 54% into the print.

evidence.text: The Iran-Gulf war, which Sprinklr's 10-Q says caused 'inaccessibility, and potential loss, of certain customer data' at a third-party UAE data centre and which management sized on 4 June as $3-4m of slipped deals plus 54 customers force-migrated to Ireland, escalated again INSIDE the reported quarter (Iranian missiles and drones fired at Gulf states on 2026-07-12) and hostilities resumed on 2026-08-31 - against a guide that assumed 'improvements in the coming quarters', with 44% of FY26 revenue generated outside the Americas.
evidence.why_not_priced: The March 1 AWS me-central-1 strike and its Q2 cost were disclosed and guided for on 4 June and are priced; the July 12 re-escalation and the 31 August resumption both post-date the guide, and with three EPS estimates on the name there is no evidence anyone re-cut a Middle East assumption - if they had, the average price target would have moved off $7.88, which it has not since Citi's June cut to $6. evidence.text: On the 2026-06-08 Q1 call [THE COMPANY]'s CFO said 'For the IEEPA tariffs of approximately $12 million paid last year, we have applied for refunds but have not included any potential benefit in the results this quarter or in the full year guidance' - a windfall equal to ~8.7% of the $138M market cap and ~$0.32/share that is carried at zero in the affirmed FY2026 adjusted-EBITDA guide of $28-32M and in the single sell-side estimate of $(0.05), and [THE COMPANY]'s Q2 ended 2026-08-02, i.e. inside the window in which the rest of retail actually booked these refunds.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no option chain at all, one analyst estimate, and 46k shares a day of volume, so there is no preview note and no vehicle through which this could be expressed. More decisively, the tape did the opposite of pricing it: [THE COMPANY] fell from a $4.27 August high to $3.62 and is -13.4% over 20 days, drifting down straight through the exact window (Target's $994M refund on 2026-08-20, Ross's $253M on 2026-08-27, CNBC's sector piece on 2026-08-30) when the tariff-refund windfall was the dominant retail-earnings story. If the market had connected a $138M-cap importer sitting on a $12M refund claim to that trade, the run-up would be positive and the stock would not be near the bottom of its August range. The disclosure exists only as one sentence of CFO prepared remarks on a June call; it is not in the Q1 press release headline items and it is in no aggregator's number - [THE COMPANY]'s own affirmed guidance and the lone $(0.05) estimate both carry it at zero, which is what 'not priced' looks like in the only two published figures that exist for this name.

And the mechanism timing is independent again: CBP's CAPE refund process opened 2026-04-20 with a stated 60-90 day turnaround once a declaration is accepted, per NRF on 2026-04-30 ([url removed] which places a claim [THE COMPANY] had already filed by 2026-06-08 squarely inside its own Q2. These are three different documents from three different filers, none of them the [THE COMPANY] transcript.

evidence.text: The 50% Section 338 tariff on Canadian imports that took DOO from C$93.82 to C$83.67 between 21 and 26 August explicitly does not apply to goods already subject to Section 232 duties - and BRP's snowmobiles and 'the majority of ORV models' have been Section 232 derivative articles at 25% of full value since 6 April 2026, by BRP's own disclosure.
evidence.source_date: 2026-08-22 (effective date stated in document; Section 338 took effect 12:01am ET 22 Aug 2026)
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market had worked through the non-stacking carve-out, DOO would not have tracked Magna one-for-one on 24 August (DOO -5.94%, Magna -6.56%) when Magna IS the Section 232 auto/parts complex and BRP is Mexico-origin recreational vehicles already inside Section 232. And the gap would have closed over the following six sessions as trade counsel published the annex analyses - instead DOO closed 2 Sep at 85.90, still 8.4% below the 21 Aug close. A targeted search for any note, wire item or trade-press piece connecting BRP to the Section 232 exclusion returned nothing: BRP has issued no release since 18 August and its next scheduled communication is tomorrow's 09:00 EDT call. Coverage that had priced this would read 'BRP largely exempt from Section 338'; no such sentence exists.
evidence.independence: Holland & Knight, a separate firm, states the same exclusion independently and adds that the proclamation named for 'motor vehicles' does not in fact reach vehicles because they are already under Section 232 (https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/07/50-percent-opening-bid-canadian-imports-subject-to-section-338-tariffs). Separately, the Globe and Mail documents that ~75% of BRP units are produced across four Mexican facilities in Juarez and Queretaro with 60% of output sold in the US, so the Canada-origin share of US-bound volume is a minority regardless of the carve-out (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-us-tariffs-turn-ski-doo-maker-brps-mexico-production-hub-into-a/, 2025-02-03).

evidence.text: BRP has never once mentioned an IEEPA tariff refund - not in the Q1 FY27 call, not in the FY26 financial statements - while Polaris booked US$74m of IEEPA refunds in the exactly-overlapping quarter with ~US$40m more pending, and BRP's own FY26 tariff drag was described as falling 'mainly on PA&A', the Asia-sourced, IEEPA-dutiable and therefore refundable part of its cost base.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus of $(0.46) sits exactly on BRP's own 28 May guidance of 'earnings to decline by approximately CAD 1.60 to CAD 1.65 year-over-year' - an estimate anchored purely to the Section 232 cost and set before CBP's refund channel, which opened 20 April 2026, had processed anything. Q2 FY27 (1 May - 31 Jul) is BRP's first full quarter inside that window. If the street had modelled a recovery, at least one estimate in a four-estimate sample would sit above the company's own guide rather than on it, and BRP's coverage would frame the name as an IEEPA refund beneficiary rather than exclusively as a Section 232 victim. Every BRP note is about the CAD 500-550m Section 232 number; none is about the refundable pre-February tariff base.
evidence.independence: Different company, different document, same refund channel: the Polaris transcript is the evidence that the mechanism is live and being recognised in this exact calendar quarter, and it is independent of BRP's own disclosure. BRP's side of it is the absence in its own Q1 FY27 transcript (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-brp-inc-q1-2027-surpasses-forecasts-stock-rises-93CH-4714754, 2026-05-28), which mentions no refund, no IEEPA, no Supreme Court and no drawback. Note this finding shares a theme (tariffs) with finding 1 but no source and no legal instrument - Section 338 and IEEPA refunds are separate.

evidence.text: BRP's model-year 2027 ORV price sheet, revealed with the 17 August product launch, holds price increases near 1% and outright lowers prices on selected Can-Am Commander, Defender and Outlander models while adding factory-installed content - i.e. BRP is absorbing the 25% ad valorem tariff in margin rather than pricing it, and its CAD 200m mitigation plan is overhead and lean initiatives, not price.
evidence.source_date: 2026-08 (published after BRP's 17 Aug 2026 MY27 reveal; article headline and body describe the MY27 price sheet)
evidence.why_not_priced: The actual MY27 price sheet exists only in powersports trade press; it is on no terminal and in no wire preview, which carry the guidance range and the consensus loss instead. If it were priced, H2 gross-margin estimates would already be pinned to the bottom of the CAD 925-975m EBITDA guide and TD would not have moved the name to Buy on 18 August. Cuts against my two positive findings, which is why I keep it.
evidence.independence: Partly confirmatory rather than new: the Globe and Mail's 28 May report on the guidance restoration already recorded that BRP planned 'no major U.S. pricing changes' and that the CAD 200m mitigation was overhead and travel (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-brp-restores-financial-outlook-expects-major-profit-hit-amid-us-tariff/, 2026-05-28). The August price sheet is the confirmation, not the announcement, so I have sized it small and flag that it should not be counted as a second independent margin datapoint.

evidence.why_not_priced: The sweep found a single $0.03 EPS estimate on this name - there is no sell-side machine tracking which CAPE phase disbursed when, and no WOOF note or wire item connects BARK's 6 August Phase-II disclosure to Petco's quarter. Petco's CFO quantified the direct exposure at ~7% of total merchandise COGS sourced from China/Canada/Mexico for owned brands, i.e. roughly $200M of annual import cost, so the residual refund is plausibly high-single to low-double-digit millions against a $110-112M Q2 adjusted EBITDA guide. Risk to the finding: BARK excluded its refund from adjusted EBITDA, and Petco could do the same or book it in Q3 - hence the wide band.
evidence.independence: Petco's own June-3 release states the exclusion verbatim ('our outlook assumes the benefit of a partial IEEPA tariff refund received in May 2026, with no additional refunds assumed for the balance of the year') - https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/petco-reports-first-quarter-2026-results-302790636.html (2026-06-03); the CAPE Phase 2 / Phase 3 timeline and the $40bn+ disbursed by end-June is independently documented at https://www.thompsonhinesmartrade.com/2026/06/cbp-announces-phases-2-and-3-of-the-ieepa-tariff-refund-process/ and https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/06/ieepa-tariff-refund-update-government-appeals (2026-06-15); the 7% exposure figure is from CFO Sabrina Simmons via https://www.retaildive.com/news/petco-reaffirms-guidance-sales-fall-q1-tariffs/750114 (2025-06-09). NOTE: this finding and finding 2 both bear on the same June-3 Petco guidance paragraph, but the external evidence is entirely separate (CBP/BARK vs EIA/BTS diesel) - collapse the Petco release, not the two findings.

evidence.text: Petco's FY2026 guide is pinned to 'fuel prices remain elevated at approximately those experienced in the first quarter' - fiscal Q1 (Feb-Apr) averaged about $4.71/gal diesel on BTS monthlies ($3.72 / $4.92 / $5.50), fiscal Q2 (May-Jul) averaged about $5.20, and diesel was $5.599/gal on 31 Aug with US diesel cracks setting an all-time record above $106/bbl on 1 Sep and record-low seasonal distillate stocks going into heating season - leaving the stated H2 assumption roughly 19% below spot.
evidence.why_not_priced: Petco names fuel as one of only two quantified guidance assumptions, so it is material enough to move the FY $415-430M adjusted EBITDA range, yet no WOOF-specific coverage carries a diesel number. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be trading with two Buy-side target actions in the last two weeks and no preview flagging the assumption as stale; the run-up of -10.5% over 20 days is too small and too undifferentiated to be this. Fiscal Q2 fuel was already inside the Q2 guide (management said the May refund would be 'approximately offset by incremental tariffs and higher fuel costs'), so the live risk is the H2/FY guide, not the Q2 print - which is why the band is wide and the upper bound is only mildly positive.
evidence.independence: Monthly BTS diesel prints corroborate the level series independently of EIA weeklies: March $4.92 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-march-2026-0), April $5.50 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-april-2026-0), May $5.60 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-may-2026-0), July $4.96 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-july-2026-0). The record-crack / distillate-squeeze context is separately reported at https://oilprice.com/Latest-Energy-News/World-News/Diesel-Cracks-Hit-Record-Highs-as-Global-Fuel-Squeeze-Deepens.html and https://rbnenergy.com/daily-posts/blog/100bbl-diesel-crack-or-how-2026-exposed-fragility-global-refining (Sept 2026). If it were priced, Petco's Q2 net sales guide of 'up about 0.3%, in line with consensus' would be treated as a floor rather than a ceiling, and WOOF would not have drifted lower against two upgraded pet-category guides.

evidence.text: Q1 FY27 consensus revenue is $237.99M, roughly 7% below what Methode's own disclosed FY27 building blocks imply for the quarter (Q1 FY26 base of $240.5M, plus the guided data-centre ramp from ~$80M to ~$130M i.e. ~+$12M/quarter, plus North American automotive going from $182M to ~$200M), and the same model was at $238.46M against a $298.1M actual last quarter and $224.57M against a $240.5M actual in the year-ago quarter.
evidence.why_not_priced: The estimate is the priced number - what is not priced is that it is structurally stale. Only 6 analysts cover a $668M-cap name and the model has sat at $238-240M per quarter through a period when management raised the full-year revenue guide to $1,025-1,075M (implying a $256-269M quarterly average) and disclosed a +$50M data-centre step-up. If the market had reflected the building blocks, the estimate would have moved with the June guide instead of staying within $0.5M of the estimate that a $298.1M quarter beat by 25%, and Baird ($16) and Sidoti ($17) would not both still carry targets below the $18.71 spot. Note this beat is NOT the recovery revenue repeating: my $252-260M figure excludes recoveries, and last quarter's $298.1M less its $22.5M of recoveries was still a 15.6% beat.
evidence.independence: Two independent methods land on the same ~$255M: the historical beat rate applied to consensus (+7.1% in the year-ago quarter, +15.6% underlying last quarter) and the bottom-up segment build. The segment build inputs are corroborated from a separate 2026-06-26 write-up of the Q4 slide deck: https://ph.investing.com/news/company-news/methode-q4-fy26-slides-transformation-drives-60-ebitda-growth-93CH-2466855 . Shares the Q4 FY26 release/transcript document cluster with findings 2 and 3.

evidence.text: Every external datapoint bearing on Methode's two growth lines post-dates the 25 June guide: hyperscaler 2026 capex was raised across the board in late July (Amazon $200B to $220B, Alphabet $180-190B to $195-205B, Meta narrowed up), and GM raised its own FY26 EBIT guidance by $500M on 21 July while running Flint Assembly six days a week from June on heavy-duty pickup demand - while Methode's data-centre number is built only on existing vendor-managed busbar volume with the 800VDC rack architecture explicitly excluded from guidance by management.
evidence.why_not_priced: Hyperscaler capex itself is the most-covered fact in the market and I am not claiming it is unpriced. The unpriced part is the specific timing asymmetry in Methode's guide: management set the $130M data-centre number and the $72-82M EBITDA range on 25 June, before those raises, and said on the call that 'when we reference the future technology and the 800-volt architectures, none of that is in our guide.' That means the guide has one-sided slack and the print has no mechanism to falsify the 800VDC thesis that drove the Craig-Hallum initiation - the bear catalyst most people would expect here cannot actually occur at the guidance level this early. If the market had connected the two, the July capex raises would have moved MEI at the time; they did not - the stock only moved on 24 August on a boutique initiation, a month later.
evidence.independence: GM's own 21 July guidance raise and the Flint six-day schedule are separate corroboration from a different industry: https://investor.gm.com/news-releases/news-release-details/gm-releases-2026-second-quarter-results and https://www.cbtnews.com/gm-to-add-sixth-production-day-at-flint-assembly/ (dated 2026-03-30, confirming the June 2026 start, cross-checked against https://usautosblog.com/2026/05/18/gm-brings-heavy-duty-pickup-inventory-home-to-feed-hungry-u-s-buyers/ dated 2026-05-18). I have deliberately sized the GM leg near zero because Methode's FY26 10-K shows its largest customer at only 10.9% of sales and the top five at 41%, so the truck tailwind is worth single-digit millions of revenue at most. The 800VDC exclusion shares the Q4 transcript with findings 1 and 3.

evidence.text: Q4 FY26's headline was inflated by $22.5M of non-recurring customer recoveries recognised as revenue, so adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M on 24.2% gross margin sat on roughly $275.6M of underlying revenue and only single-digit-millions of underlying EBITDA; management said recovery activity is 'largely done' and excluded the remaining balance from FY27 guidance, so this print delivers the year's worst sequential optics - revenue down ~15% and EBITDA down sharply from Q4 - into a stock at a 52-week high.
evidence.why_not_priced: This one is mostly priced and I am filing it at residual size only, because the +14.23 vol points of 25-delta put skew is exactly what a market braced for a trough quarter after a recovery-inflated comp looks like. The residual that is not priced is the composition detail: the $22.5M is disclosed as revenue, not as an EBITDA add-back, so a reader working from adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M and a 24.2% gross margin will not see how thin the underlying run-rate was, and the ~45% sequential EBITDA decline that follows mechanically will read as deterioration rather than as arithmetic. This is compatible with finding 1 rather than contradicting it - a revenue beat alongside weak EBITDA is precisely what March 2026 printed, and the stock fell 12-15% on that combination.
evidence.independence: The $45M negotiated / $22.5M recognised split is confirmed independently at https://ph.investing.com/news/company-news/methode-q4-fy26-slides-transformation-drives-60-ebitda-growth-93CH-2466855 (2026-06-26). evidence.text: Exactly one year ago Methode postponed this same fiscal quarter's release on the scheduled release day - 3 September 2025, having pre-announced 3 September on 21 August 2025 - gave no reason whatsoever in the reschedule notice, and the stock fell 11.4% the following session; it then reported six days later, on 9 September 2025, with a revenue beat ($240.5M vs $224.57M) and an EPS beat (-$0.22 vs -$0.40).

It is a fiscal-Q1-specific close-process fragility with a documented 11.4% price consequence, and a repeat would be announced within hours of now. If the market carried it, the front-expiry chain would not be implying only a 7.4% event move on a name whose last three prints and pre-print notices produced -11.4%, -12 to -15% and +23.7%. I am sizing this as an expected value on a low-probability tail, not as a forecast that it recurs; the company filed no NT 10-Q and the 2025 outcome was benign.

evidence.why_not_priced: The wire framing of the June print is 'net sales up 15.9%, topped estimates by 25%, adjusted EBITDA beat by nearly 60%' with no adjustment for the $22.5M of recoveries, and the stock's +140% YTD re-rating was built on that framing. evidence.text: The Q2 FY27 consensus of $2.68 EPS / $297.8M revenue has been unchanged for 60 days - i.e. it was never re-based after Q1 printed $3.24 vs $1.82 (+78%) and $291.0M vs $249.4M (+16.7%) - and it implies revenue up only 2.3% sequentially and EPS down 17% sequentially in Argan's seasonally strongest construction quarter, while the same analysts' FY27 annual estimate ($1.28B revenue, $12.09 EPS, 5 analysts, as of 2026-08-26) requires ~$330M and ~$2.95 per quarter across Q2-Q4.
evidence.why_not_priced: The wire will print '$2.68 expected' and every screen will compare to it. What is not priced is that the quarterly and annual estimates from the same five analysts are mutually inconsistent by ~10% on revenue for this specific quarter: nobody reconciles a stale, 2-estimate quarterly stub against a 5-estimate annual number. If the market had reconciled them, the Q2 estimate would have drifted up in the 60 days since the Q1 blowout instead of sitting flat, and the FY26 sequential pattern (Q1 $193.7M to Q2 $237.7M, +22.7%) would have been reflected in a Q2 number above $320M rather than $297.8M.
evidence.independence: stockanalysis.com's forecast page carries the FY27 annual consensus of $1.28B revenue and $12.09 EPS on 5 analysts, as of 2026-08-26 - a different source from the Zacks quarterly stub, and the arithmetic residual ($1.28B less Q1's actual $291.0M, over three quarters) is what makes the quarterly bar look low: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/agx/forecast/

evidence.text: Short interest is 1.02M shares - 7.38% of float and 3.28 days to cover as of the 2026-09-02 data date - on only 14.02M shares outstanding, and days-to-cover is up 65% year over year; the position was built during a 33% 20-day drawdown that the only article addressing it attributes entirely to a sector reassessment with no Argan-specific news.
evidence.why_not_priced: Short interest is not a directional forecast, so this is a convexity claim, not a view: on a 14.0M-share company with 277k shares of daily volume, 1.02M shares short is 3.3 sessions of covering demand that has to transact in the session after the print. If the market had priced the squeeze risk, the 25-delta skew would be negative (calls bid) rather than +2.6 with downside paid, and the front-expiry open interest would not be sitting at only 8,200 contracts with a 20%-of-mid ATM spread. Instead the chain is call-heavy on open interest (0.31 put/call) but put-bid on vol - an inconsistency that says the chain is illiquid rather than informed.
evidence.independence: Different source, same direction on the 'washed out without cause' leg: the 2026-08-29 Yahoo piece states the fall came 'amid a broad selloff across engineering and construction stocks' and names no Argan-specific trigger, and puts the P/E at 36.3x against an industry 32.5x - https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/argan-agx-undervalued-sector-led-061615421.html . This finding shares no document with finding 1.

evidence.text: In a Q1 10-Q footnote, contract liabilities (customer billings and advances ahead of cost) rose to $565.8M at 2026-04-30 from $514.0M at 2026-01-31 while $222.6M of revenue was recognised out of that balance - implying roughly $274M of fresh customer cash advanced in a quarter that recognised $291M of revenue, against contract assets of only $36.9M.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the single best leading indicator Argan discloses - customers do not prepay nearly two quarters of revenue on work they are about to stop - and it sits in a revenue-recognition footnote that no aggregator carries and that a five-analyst coverage list does not model. The August de-rating was a bet that the power-EPC order and spend cycle is rolling over; had anyone priced this footnote, the drawdown would not have been indiscriminate with the E&C group, and the sell-side notes cited in the wire (Zacks to Hold 08-07, Weiss cut 08-11) would have argued about funded backlog rather than about ratings.
evidence.independence: Corroborated in a different document by the same filer, so treat as one cluster: the 2026-06-04 earnings release reports cash and investments of $973.6M with zero debt, which is the balance-sheet consequence of the advance build - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100591/000110465926070517/agx-20260604xex99d1.htm . evidence.text: Backlog has now declined for two straight quarters from its peak - RUPO of $3.0B at 2026-10-31 per the Q3 10-Q, $2.9B at 2026-01-31, $2.8B at 2026-04-30 - and Argan has press-released and 8-K'd zero new power EPC awards in the three months since the Q1 call, the only 8-K being an $8.3M teledata bolt-on (ValCor, 2026-08-04), against management's Q1 guidance of 'a handful of new projects over the next 10 to 18 months' and add-on backlog additions of only ~$125M in Q1; on ~$320-350M of Q2 revenue that makes a third consecutive sequential decline to roughly $2.6-2.7B the likely headline.
evidence.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is doable by anyone but the inputs are scattered across a 10-Q RUPO note, an earnings release, an absence of 8-Ks and a call transcript, and with five analysts nobody publishes it. What is genuinely mispriced is the framing: the wire narrative on AGX is 'record revenue, record backlog', and the Oct-2025 $3.0B peak is not the number quoted anywhere in current coverage. I size this smaller than the bear case looks because the baseline's own history contradicts the reflex: the +37.91% print on 2026-03-26 came with backlog DOWN sequentially from $3.0B to $2.9B, and the -11.98% print on 2025-12-04 came with a RECORD $3.0B backlog. evidence.independence: The zero-award leg is independently visible in the company's own EDGAR filing record for CIK 0000100591 between 2026-06-04 and 2026-09-02 (only 8-Ks are the 06-10 dividend and the 08-04 ValCor acquisition): https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000100591&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40 . evidence.text: Two state-level restrictions on data-center grid interconnection landed after Argan last spoke to investors on 2026-06-04 - Abbott ordered PUCT/ERCOT to audit data centers before approving new connections and ERCOT paused its 'batch zero' review (2026-08-03), and Pennsylvania restricted data-center permitting (2026-08-18, on which Talen fell 11%) - but the Texas order explicitly exempts data centers with on-site power generation, which is precisely the dedicated behind-the-meter gas plant Gemma builds.
evidence.why_not_priced: The market traded AGX as an undifferentiated data-center-capex derivative through August. The specific carve-out - grid connection frozen, on-site generation exempt - channels hyperscaler demand toward exactly Argan's product in exactly Argan's biggest market (both mega-projects in backlog are ERCOT). If this had been priced, AGX would have decoupled from the IPP and grid-connected names in the 08-18 to 08-29 leg instead of falling with them. I keep the sign slightly negative only because management now has to answer pipeline questions for the first time with this as the backdrop, and the timeline has already compressed once.

evidence.text: US Mint American Eagle silver bullion sales in Gold.com's fiscal Q4 (Apr/May/Jun 2026) were 380,500 / 0 / 260,000 coins = 640,500, down 76% from the year-ago quarter's 2,620,000 (1,530,000 / 775,000 / 315,000) and down 92% from Q3 FY26's 8,180,000, with May 2026 the first calendar month of zero bullion Silver Eagle sales in the program's 40-year history - and Gold.com is both a Mint Authorized Purchaser and, since consolidating Sunshine Minting on 2026-04-02, the owner of the Mint's primary silver blank supplier.
evidence.source_date: 2026 (May-2026 data month; date verified independently - see independence)
evidence.why_not_priced: The Mint publishes this monthly in a CSV that no financial aggregator maps onto GOLD, and the sell-side is visibly modelling the gold price instead: a $70 target was reaffirmed on 2026-08-27, five analysts average $65.80 against a $43.66 spot (+42%), and Zacks ran GOLD as Bull of the Day. If this were in the price, the 25-delta skew would not be +0.59 vol points (effectively flat) and open interest would not be 0.29 puts per call - that is call-dominated positioning, the opposite of a market braced for a retail-volume print. The zero month also lands in the same quarter Gold.com bought the blank supplier whose flagship order book it emptied, which is a fact no wire story has connected.
evidence.independence: Date and magnitude corroborated from two different sources: coinnews.net puts YTD-through-June 2026 bullion Silver Eagle sales at roughly 8.8 million ounces, which matches the six monthly figures summing to 8,820,500 exactly (https://www.coinnews.net/2026/07/02/silver-eagle-soars-in-return/, URL path /2026/07/), and a second outlet reports the May zero with 2026 in its URL path (https://atlantagoldandcoin.com/us-mint-zero-silver-eagle-sales-may-2026/). The 2025 comparison months come from the US Mint's own tidy CSV (https://www.usmint.gov/content/dam/usmint/data/tidy/bullion-american-eagle-silver.csv).

evidence.text: The retail premium over spot on 1oz American Silver Eagles - which is Gold.com's actual revenue per ounce, not the metal price - peaked at 19.16% on 2026-02-17 inside fiscal Q3, then fell to a 5.30% low on 2026-04-24, 6.69% on 2026-05-25 and a ~7.93% June average across fiscal Q4, and has kept falling in the current quarter: 8.48% average in July 2026 against 6.87% in August 2026.
evidence.why_not_priced: Gold.com's own Q3 release states Direct-to-Consumer contributed 67% of gross profit, so gross profit is premium x ounces - yet every piece of published coverage keys off the gold price (gold rose ~10% in August) and off the Q3 headline of $10.35bn revenue and $2.09 EPS. A ~19% premium on ~$80 silver is roughly $15/oz of spread; a 6% premium on ~$69 silver is roughly $4/oz. If the market had focused on this, the August reaffirmation of a $70 price target and the FY27 $4.09 EPS anchor would have been cut instead, and the 20-day run-up would not still be +2.27%. The August print at 6.87%, below July's 8.48%, is the part that matters most because it prices the FY27 outlook management gives on tonight's call, not the quarter already ended.
evidence.independence: Same publisher as finding 1 but a different dataset (dealer ask prices vs Mint unit sales) - flagging the source-cluster overlap explicitly. Independent directional corroboration of collapsed premiums from a third party: as of 2026-08-26, silver spot $68.57 with 100oz bars and 90% junk silver quoted at -4.8% (below spot) and 1oz coins at ~0.7% over spot on the lowest-premium screen (https://www.kellergoldandsilver.com/post/why-is-the-buyback-price-for-silver-so-much-lower-than-the-spot-price-right-now-2026-guide).

evidence.text: Third-party e-commerce estimates put jmbullion.com revenue at $66.4M in July 2026 and down 24% over the trailing three months versus the preceding three months, while Similarweb's July 2026 data shows the site's global rank deteriorating from 18,648 to 20,259 over three months and traffic down 3% month-on-month.
evidence.why_not_priced: JM Bullion is 27% of Q3 gross profit on the company's own disclosure and is not separately tracked by any sell-side model; alternative-data panels on a private-brand website are not in wire copy and not in the single published EPS estimate. If the market were watching DTC order flow rather than the gold price, the 5-day run of -6.8% would not sit against a 20-day run of +2.27% and a call-heavy option book. This is an estimate from a panel, not a company disclosure, which is why it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Yes - a different vendor with a different methodology points the same way: Similarweb's jmbullion.com page (https://www.similarweb.com/website/jmbullion.com/, July 2026 data). Both are independent of the US Mint volume series and the dealer premium series in findings 1 and 2.

evidence.text: The company's own nine-month numbers imply extreme operating leverage that makes the lone $0.96 Q4 estimate fragile: 9M gross profit $342.8M less Q3's $176.6M leaves $166.2M for H1, and 9M net income $70.2M less Q3's $59.5M leaves just $10.7M - so at an H1-like ~$83M quarterly gross profit the business earns roughly $0.19 a quarter, against a Q4 cost base now carrying Q3's $78M SG&A plus a full quarter of consolidated Sunshine Minting and $19M+ of quarterly interest.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is arithmetic on a public release rather than a discovery, but with only one published Q4 estimate the arithmetic has visibly not been done: Zacks' 2026-02-11 note carried FY27 EPS of $4.09 (~$1.02 a quarter) and FY26 estimates raised 50% in 60 days, which extrapolates the premium-spike quarter as a run-rate. If the H1-to-Q3 gross profit swing had been recognised as a premium cycle rather than a level, targets 42-60% above spot would not have been reaffirmed on 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-27.
evidence.independence: none - this rests on the same Q3 release as the segment mix cited in findings 2 and 3, and should be collapsed into that source cluster rather than counted twice. The FY27 $4.09 anchor it argues against is separately sourced: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/bull-day-goldcom-gold (2026-02-11).

Global bar-and-coin gold demand fell 36% sequentially to 307.1t in calendar Q2 2026 from 476.8t in Q1 -- and those are precisely the two quarters that map to Gold.com's fiscal Q4 (the quarter being reported, one estimate at $0.96) and fiscal Q3 (which printed $2.09), while retail premium spreads simultaneously troughed at multi-year lows and US Mint Silver Eagle bullion orders from Authorized Purchasers, of which A-Mark is one, hit exactly zero in May 2026.
evidence.why_not_priced: This company's operating leverage is extreme and unmodelled by a one-estimate consensus: fiscal Q2 FY26 gross profit of $93.4m produced EPS of $0.46 while fiscal Q3's $176.6m produced $2.09, so an $83m gross-profit swing moved EPS by $1.63. Reverting Q4 gross profit toward the Q2 level on 36% lower volumes and compressed spreads puts EPS near $0.45-0.65, not $0.96. If the market had focused on this, the 20-day run-up would not be +2.3% -- the stock rose with gold through July and August while the volume and premium regime that actually sets its margin went the other way, which is the signature of a shareholder base pricing metal beta rather than dealer spread. There is also no sell-side preview to have carried it: coverage is effectively a single estimate, and the CEO's own Q2 FY26 language about 'tight' premium spreads in a quarter with better volumes than this one has never been connected to the Q4 setup in any published note.
evidence.independence: Two further sources point the same way from different data: US Mint Authorized Purchaser orders for 1oz Silver Eagle bullion were zero for the whole of May 2026, the first full-month zero since the 1986 launch, with only ~260,000 in June (https://findbullionprices.com/blog/silver-eagle-sales-hit-zero-in-may-2026-the-retail-buyer-has-left/, corroborated independently at https://atlantagoldandcoin.com/us-mint-zero-silver-eagle-sales-may-2026/ -- both return 403 to automated fetch, so snippet-only); and Silver Eagle premium history shows the low print of 6.69% on 2026-05-25 against a ~19.2% peak earlier in 2026 (https://findbullionprices.com/premium-history/silver-coins/American-Silver-Eagle-Monster-Box-Random-Year/, snippet-only). A-Mark's Authorized Purchaser status is confirmed at https://www.usmint.gov/coins-precious-metal-coins/bullion-authorized-purchasers/. These are volume measures and a price measure respectively, so they are not restatements of the World Gold Council tonnage.

evidence.text: The baseline's two-print reaction history is half contaminated: the +9.87% move attributed to the 2026-02-05 amc earnings release was in fact the same-evening 4:10pm ET announcement of a $150m Tether PIPE at $44.50 with a board seat, alongside EPS of only $0.46 -- leaving 2026-05-06 (+0.95% on a sequential EPS jump from $0.46 to $2.09) as the only clean earnings reaction this registrant has produced.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a magnitude constraint, not a direction. The chain's 8.87% event-implied move and the baseline's 5.41% median absolute reaction both rest on treating February as an earnings reaction. Strip it and the demonstrated EPS-print sensitivity of this name is about one percent: the market was handed a 4.5x sequential EPS beat in May and moved the stock less than a point, because it correctly read the windfall as non-recurring. If the option market had made this adjustment, the ATM straddle would not be quoted with a bid-ask 62% of mid on 8,448 total open interest -- that width is what an uninterrogated volatility mark looks like. The market prices this stock off deals and narrative, which is exactly why the contamination happened in the first place.
evidence.independence: The two-print history and the +0.95% May figure come from the sealed baseline, so the only genuinely independent leg is the release timestamp itself. The Q2 FY26 EPS of $0.46 that the +9.87% was mistakenly attributed to is at https://ir.gold.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/215/gold-com-reports-fiscal-second-quarter-2026-results (2026-02-05). Note this finding and finding 3 both lean on the 'market ignores this company's EPS line' reading of the same May 6 reaction -- treat them as one source cluster on that point.

evidence.text: Gold closed fiscal Q4 at $4,007.69 on 30 June 2026 and then rallied above $4,700 by 24 August -- its first move above $4,600 since 15 May -- before giving back 5.62% in the final week of August, and Silver Eagle premiums recovered from the 6.69% May trough to an 8.57% July average; so management reports a dead quarter into a rising, volatile one that resembles the regime that generated fiscal Q3's $2.09.
evidence.why_not_priced: Gold's own level is obviously priced -- it is the most public number in the world, and GOLD's -6.8% five-day fade is simply beta to last week's 5.6% metal drop. What is not priced is the release's framing: this is a fiscal Q4 *and full-year* print in which the full year goes from $0.71 to roughly $3.20 in EPS and gross profit from $210.9m to roughly $450m, so the headline reads as a record by a factor of four while the soft quarter only appears in a sequential comparison that a one-analyst tape will be slow to compute. Had the market focused on the quarter rather than the year, the mildly positive 25-delta skew of +0.59 vol points would be materially wider on the put side than a flat market's half-point.
evidence.independence: Independent corroboration of the July-August gold recovery and the late-August reversal at https://www.forbes.com/advisor/investing/gold-price/ (2026-08-31). The FY25 comparison base of $0.71 EPS and $210.9m gross profit is at https://ir.gold.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/206/a-mark-precious-metals-reports-fiscal-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results (2025-09-09). Shares the May 6 reaction reading with finding 2 -- see the note there.

evidence.text: NSSF-adjusted NICS for SWBI's exact fiscal Q1 (May+June+July 2026) totalled 3,290,647 against 3,055,402 a year earlier, +7.70% y/y - a 6.5-point acceleration from the +1.20% in the Feb-Apr quarter on which SWBI just printed revenue +26.7% and handgun sell-in +23.2%, while consensus looks for only +16% revenue growth off an $85.1M base.
evidence.why_not_priced: The July single-month headline (+8.5%) was NSSF-press-released and is in the wire, but the three-month fiscal-quarter aggregate and the bridge from it to SWBI's own realised sell-in ratio is published nowhere. The validation is that the company's Q4 release cited 'NICS increased only 1.1%' for Feb-Apr and my computed figure for that window is +1.20% - so this identical series, one quarter later, is the number management will read out tonight, and it is six points better. If the street had run this arithmetic the sell-side revenue bar would not sit 11 points BELOW the growth the company delivered last quarter on a demand backdrop six points weaker, and the stock would not be -16.35% over 20 sessions with 25-delta call skew (-0.67) into the print.
evidence.independence: Sturm Ruger's 2026-07-29 release, filed after SWBI last spoke, reports estimated distributor-to-retailer sell-through of its own products +19% in Apr-Jun (two of SWBI's three months) against adjusted NICS +5%: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729922943/en/Sturm-Ruger-Company-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results . Ruger's cited NICS comparator derives from the same NSSF series as this finding; the sell-through and unit-inventory figures do not.

evidence.text: Both channel layers turned positive in SWBI's exact quarter, and both datapoints were published after SWBI last spoke: Ruger's distributor inventories fell 45,800 units and finished goods 100,100 units on sell-through +19% (2026-07-29), and Sportsman's Warehouse's 10-Q for the 13 weeks ended 2026-08-01 shows firearm sales +$5.2M / +8.7% and ammunition +$3.9M / +9.9% (filed 2026-09-01).
evidence.why_not_priced: SWBI's last guidance-bearing statement was 2026-06-17, when it framed FY2027 industry demand as 'slightly higher' than FY2026. Both of these prints post-date that and both are better than 'slightly higher', and channel de-stock has been the bear case on SWBI for six quarters - the paragraph that would move the stock is the channel-inventory paragraph, not EPS. Visible evidence it is not priced: SWBI fell 7.97% in the five sessions that contain SPWH's 2026-09-01 print, on which SPWH shares rose - a same-category retailer's firearms acceleration was published and SWBI's equity went the other way.
evidence.independence: Independent of the NICS series and of finding 1's mechanism - these are physical unit inventories at a distributor and dollar comps at a retailer, from two different filers. Ruger source: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729922943/en/Sturm-Ruger-Company-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results . Caveat that cuts the other way: SPWH reaffirmed rather than raised FY guidance (-1.0% to +2.0% comps, $30-36M EBITDA) in its 2026-09-01 release, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/01/3354585/30783/en/sportsman-s-warehouse-holdings-inc-announces-second-quarter-2026-financial-results.html

evidence.text: On 2026-08-05 the N.D. Texas entered final judgment and a permanent injunction in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF holding NFA registration of suppressors/SBRs/SBSs unconstitutional after the tax went to zero; the stay expired 2026-08-12 and DOJ declined an emergency appeal - three weeks after SWBI's 2026-07-15 investor day told investors suppressors were its fastest-growing lane at +95.6% revenue growth in H1 CY2026 into a $700M-$950M TAM, with July NFA-category NICS checks +108.8% y/y to 130,013.
evidence.why_not_priced: The entire coverage set for this ruling is gun-law media, NRA-ILA and law-firm client alerts; not one financial-press item in my searches connects it to SWBI, and the SWBI preview copy in the wire is pure consensus revenue/EPS. It is also a forward item - it post-dates the printed quarter - so it can only enter the price through tonight's call, where management will be asked about the one growth lane it spent its investor day on. If the market had connected the two, a stock whose newest disclosed growth engine just had its principal regulatory friction enjoined would not carry -0.67 skew and a 16% 20-day de-rate.
evidence.independence: NSSF's own 2026-08-17 FFL guidance confirms the ruling is live but that the industry is in compliance limbo, which is why I band this two-sided rather than purely positive: https://www.nssf.org/articles/nssf-guidance-on-nfa-transfers/ . evidence.text: Hanwha Vision - which signed an $800m+, 10-year, multi-generation edge-AI SoC LTA with Ambarella on 2026-05-28 - reported its security segment's best quarter ever for calendar Q2 2026 (KRW 394.6bn, +20.1% YoY vs KRW 328.4bn), with AI-CCTV rising to 59% of network-camera revenue from 46% a year earlier; that AI mix shift is exactly the content-per-camera driver behind Ambarella's professional IoT line, which is ~75% of its revenue.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a Korean-language disclosure by a KRX-listed company (Hanwha Vision, 489790) published 2026-08-06. Every US-facing AMBA preview I could find is anchored on the same three numbers - consensus revenue $107.76m, non-GAAP EPS ~$0.17, and the unchanged FY27 'we're still thinking 10-15%' - and none of them mentions Hanwha Vision's own quarter. If this had been priced, you would see (a) at least one AMBA note in the four weeks after 6 August citing professional-security demand, and (b) some fundamental re-rating in the tape; instead AMBA simply retraced the takeover-rumour pop and now sits 5.4% below its last undisturbed close, i.e. the market did no fundamental work at all in that window. The $800m LTA headline itself IS priced - it was released alongside the Q1 print on 2026-05-28 and the stock still fell 21% - but the partner's subsequent operating performance is not.
evidence.independence: Arashi Vision (Insta360, 688775.SH), whose Ace/Ace Pro line runs Ambarella firmware, filed H1 2026 on 2026-08-27: revenue RMB5.52bn, +50.29% YoY, consumer smart imaging devices RMB4.788bn, +51.56% - a different downstream camera maker, different exchange, different language, pointing the same way on unit demand through Ambarella's May-July quarter. https://finance.sina.com.cn/roll/2026-08-28/doc-inipvmnh0281602.shtml . Caveat that keeps this genuinely secondary: the Ambarella-Insta360 link rests on firmware evidence (https://www.goprawn.com/forum/ambarella-cams/20635-insta360-ace-and-ace-pro-firmware-hacks) not a disclosure, and Insta360's new flagship X6 launched 2026-08-12 is described as using a 4nm 'custom chip' with no vendor named (https://petapixel.com/2026/08/12/insta360-wants-its-flagship-x6-to-be-way-more-than-a-360-degree-camera/), which if it is not Ambarella cuts the other way from Q3 onward. evidence.text: The baseline's -20.07% 20-day run-up is not a fundamental de-rate: AMBA closed $69.19 on 2026-07-29, jumped +7.08% to $74.09 on 30 July and +16.08% to $86.00 on 31 July on the FT report of NXP takeover talks, and has since bled straight back to $65.43 - only 5.4% below the last undisturbed pre-rumour close, against SMH -6.6% from 7 August to 3 September. There has been no report anywhere that the NXP process ended.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a correction to how the sealed baseline reads rather than new news, and it has two offsetting legs that I am deliberately filing as one because they rest on a single fact - the July NXP rumour. Leg one (negative, dominant): a -20% 20-day run-up, -31.5% from the 52-week high and a 2.14 put/call open-interest ratio normally say 'expectations already cut, positioning defensive, bar low'. Here none of that is true - the drawdown is a mechanical premium unwind concentrated in the six sessions after 7 August, the pre-rumour price is essentially intact beta-adjusted, and the put-heavy open interest is more plausibly deal-related option residue than a fundamental bearish bet. So the standard 'beaten-down semi bounces on an in-line print' trade is not actually set up, and anyone sizing off the baseline's run-up field will over-weight it. Leg two (positive, smaller): the market is now pricing deal probability at roughly zero even though no source reports the talks dead, leaving a live low-probability, high-payoff tail - a signed merger agreement released alongside earnings, which does happen. If the market still carried any deal probability, the stock would not have round-tripped below the undisturbed close; if it were confident the talks were dead, there would be a story saying so, and there is not.
evidence.independence: The rumour date, the +16% move and the fact the talks were unresolved are independently documented at https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ambarella-reportedly-in-talks-to-be-acquired-by-nxp-semiconductors-shares-spike-4829078 (2026-07-31). The SMH comparison comes from a separate price series, https://stockanalysis.com/etf/smh/history/ (Aug 7 $582.70 -> Sep 3 $544.39). My AMBA series reconciles exactly to the sealed baseline (65.425/81.85-1 = -20.07%, the baseline's own 20-day figure), so this is not a data disagreement, it is a reading of the same data.

Ambarella cut total manufacturing purchase commitments 33% sequentially, from $80.4m at 31-Jan-26 to $53.9m at 30-Apr-26, and booked a first-ever $1.2m adverse-purchase-commitment loss liability (it was exactly $0 the prior quarter) - while inventory rose 54% to $80.4m and days of inventory went 99 to 145, a build management told the call was precautionary against a second-half supply shortage.
evidence.why_not_priced: The two facts point opposite ways and only one of them is visible in any aggregator. Inventory and days-of-inventory are screened fields and management gave them a benign supply-insurance framing on the call; the forward commitment balance is a hand-tagged XBRL item in a commitments footnote that no data vendor carries, and it contradicts that framing - you do not cut your forward wafer book by a third if you fear a shortage, and you do not accrue for adverse commitments unless your demand forecast has fallen below your committed supply. If the market had read it, the sell side would not be sitting at a $95 consensus target with Rosenblatt at $120 and an all-Buy tape on 2026-08-31, and the stock would not have risen 38% from $62.13 on 26-Jun to $86.00 on 31-Jul on broker-note and M&A narrative in the eight weeks AFTER this 10-Q was public. evidence.text: A customer development project funded by a $13.5m cash advance was terminated on 12-May-26; $4.5m is refunded and the remaining $9.0m is XBRL-tagged as a forecast reduction of R&D expense in the quarter ended 31-Jul-26 - i.e. tonight's quarter - yet the 28-May press release and the earnings call both omitted it entirely while guiding Q2 non-GAAP opex to $56.0-59.0m against $56.4m actual in Q1.
evidence.why_not_priced: The arithmetic forces a fork the five models on this name cannot both have taken, and consensus reconciles to the naive branch. R&D is roughly four-fifths of Ambarella's opex, so a $9.0m credit is a ~20% cut to the R&D line; for reported non-GAAP opex still to land inside $56-59m the underlying run-rate would have to have jumped ~16% sequentially with zero explanation given. Consensus of a ($0.30) GAAP loss on 5 estimates bridges almost exactly off the $56-59m guide midpoint at face value, which is what you get when analysts take the guide and never open the footnote. So either the credit sits on top of the guide as an unguided ~$0.21/share benefit, or it is silently inside it and Q3 opex must step back up ~$9m - and management has said nothing that lets the market tell which. Had this been priced, at least one of the press release, the prepared remarks or the Q&A would have carried the words 'one-time' or 'credit', and none does.
evidence.independence: The non-disclosure is established by two documents separate from the 10-Q: the 28-May-26 results release, which mentions no terminated project, no deposit and neither the $13.5m nor the $9.0m - https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/28/3303255/23306/en/ambarella-inc-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results.html - and the full call transcript, in which none of those terms appears anywhere while Fermi Wang was simultaneously selling the LTA/NRE pipeline ('most of the discussion will involve NRE') - https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/ambarella-amba-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/.
