evidence.text: The stock at $65.43 is 5.4% BELOW its pre-rumour close of $69.19 on 29-Jul-26, i.e. the entire premium from the FT's 31-Jul-26 report that NXP was in talks to buy the company for over $3bn has been erased and then some, with no report anywhere that the talks collapsed - and the -20.1% 20-session slide compares with only -6.8% for SOXX over the same span, so ~13 points of it is idiosyncratic and unattributed to any dated company news.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a statement about the shape of the distribution, not a private fact, and it is the reason I am not simply stacking the -9.2% mean reaction on top of my negative fundamentals. Tonight is the first time management speaks publicly since the FT report five weeks ago, and the price implies essentially zero deal probability - if the market carried even a 20-25% chance of a >$3bn takeout the stock would not be trading below where it stood before anyone had heard of the bid. That makes the left tail self-limiting (a cheaper price makes the deal easier for a strategic acquirer who has never denied being at the table) and leaves a fat, unpriced right tail if the answer to the inevitable Q&A question is anything other than 'no comment'. If it were priced there would be a visible arb spread, a bid-supported floor and elevated call open interest; instead front-expiry total open interest is 5,641 contracts with a 2.14 put/call ratio and a 69%-of-mid ATM spread.
evidence.independence: The idiosyncratic-vs-index decomposition rests on two separate price series I pulled independently: AMBA daily closes ($69.19 on 2026-07-29, $86.00 on 2026-07-31, $81.85 on 2026-08-05) at https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/amba/history/ and SOXX daily closes (530.70 on 2026-08-05, 494.40 on 2026-09-03) at https://stockanalysis.com/etf/soxx/history/. evidence.text: US energy storage installed a record 20.2 GWh in calendar Q2 2026 (17.9-18.0 GWh utility-scale, 1.8 GWh commercial/industrial), 30.8 GWh in H1, and SEIA/Benchmark RAISED the full-year 2026 forecast to 71 GWh versus 59 GWh installed in 2025 - published 2026-09-01, twelve weeks after [THE COMPANY] last spoke, and covering the two months (May, June) that sit inside [THE COMPANY]'s fiscal Q3.
evidence.why_not_priced: [THE COMPANY]'s Technical Solutions grew 27.2% in Q2 FY26 explicitly on battery energy storage, and the entire FY26 adjusted-EPS guide rests on management's claim that 'volume will ramp meaningfully in ATS' in the back half - the single most doubted line in the guide, because ATS margin was diluted in Q2 by equipment-heavy BESS work. The datapoint that validates it sits in solar/storage trade press a week before the print, on a $2.8bn company with only three published estimates; no [THE COMPANY] preview carries it. If the market had made the connection, [THE COMPANY] would not be sitting 4.68% below its 52-week high with 15.1% annualised realised vol into a print where its fastest-growing segment's end market just set an all-time quarterly record and had its annual outlook raised 20%. Note this also refutes the Wood Mackenzie call (published 2025-07-01) that US grid-scale BESS would contract 29% in 2026 on FEOC and tariff constraints, which is the version of this story that was current when [THE COMPANY] guided.
evidence.independence: Independently reported the same day by a different trade outlet from the same SEIA/Benchmark release: [url removed] (2026-09-01). Directionally corroborated by a separate, unrelated demand channel - hyperscaler capex guidance was raised again at the late-July/early-August 2026 prints (Amazon to ~$220bn from ~$200bn, Alphabet to $195-205bn from $180-190bn) per [url removed] - which feeds the same ATS data-centre electrical book. Shares no document with any other finding in this file.

evidence.text: CBRE's Q2 2026 US office report (2026-07-29) shows national vacancy falling 30bp to 18.3% - 'the largest quarterly decline since 2015' - net absorption of 12.6m sq ft, nearly double the prior quarter and a ninth straight positive quarter, leasing +16% y/y, with CBRE projecting 2026 annual leasing to surpass the 2022 record; San Francisco, the exact market [THE COMPANY]'s CEO singled out on 2026-06-05 as having vacancy 'probably 2 or 3x worse than New York City', posted +963,980 sq ft of net absorption in the quarter.
evidence.why_not_priced: Business & Industry is ~44% of [THE COMPANY] revenue ($1,015.8m of $2,290.0m in Q2) and was flat y/y, which management attributed to UK and West Coast client exits driven by CRE weakness. The office inflection is fully priced in office REITs, which are the constituency that reads CBRE Figures; it is not priced in a janitorial contractor covered by three analysts, because the transmission runs through re-scoping, occupancy-linked hours and win rates rather than through any line an [THE COMPANY] preview models. If it were priced you would see [THE COMPANY] bid into the print rather than -3.07% over 20 days, and you would see at least one of the three estimates moving after 2026-07-29. Sized small deliberately: janitorial scope lags leasing by several quarters, and near-term reported B&I is dominated by the disclosed Transport for London exit worth ~300bp of back-half B&I growth, so this is a tone-and-FY27 item more than a Q3 revenue item.
evidence.independence: A different firm, different methodology, same direction and published separately: Colliers' Q2 2026 US office statistics report the strongest quarterly net absorption in seven years with national vacancy at ~18% - [url removed] San Francisco detail is a second CBRE document ([url removed] 2026-07-10), so treat the two CBRE files as one source cluster with Colliers as the genuinely independent leg.

evidence.text: [THE COMPANY] Aviation grew 19.5% in Q2 and its CEO warned on 2026-06-05 that 'rising fuel costs will likely create some near-term challenges for our airline clients'; since then the airline cost shock deepened rather than resolved - American Airlines cut FY26 guidance a second time in July (to a -$0.65 to +$0.65 adjusted EPS range from -$0.40 to +$1.10, with a Q3 loss guide, on ~$3.75/gal fuel), Southwest cut FY26 to $3.25-$4.25 from 'at least $4' after a ~$900m y/y Q2 fuel increase, and Alaska has had guidance suspended since April.
evidence.why_not_priced: Aviation is 13.5% of [THE COMPANY] revenue ($310.8m, $16.3m segment operating profit in Q2) and was the second-fastest-growing segment, and the market is extrapolating the Heathrow ramp. Airline distress is completely priced in airline equities - it is not priced in a name screened as defensive facility services, and none of the three published [THE COMPANY] estimates models an airline procurement squeeze on outsourced cabin, ground and passenger-assistance scope. If the market had priced it, [THE COMPANY]'s 25-delta skew would be visibly bid for downside and the stock would be more than 4.68% off its high with realised vol above 15%. Sized small on purpose and honestly: TSA throughput set records through June and July 2026 so in-quarter volumes were fine, the direct Q3 EPS arithmetic of even a 5% Aviation revenue shortfall is roughly a penny, most [THE COMPANY] airline contracts pass through labour, and the industry capacity trim was already partly visible before [THE COMPANY] guided on 2026-06-05. The risk here is to forward commentary and FY27 framing, not to the Q3 number.
evidence.independence: Partial only. BofA's carrier-capacity tracking (Q3 2026 domestic growth cut to ~0.8%, American to 7.5% from 9.3%, Delta to 1.2%) points the same way - [url removed] - but that page carries a corrupt primary timestamp and a 2026-05-26 update stamp, i.e. it may pre-date [THE COMPANY]'s guide, so I am not resting the finding on it. The [THE COMPANY]-side leg is management's own 2026-06-05 remark in the transcript: [url removed]

evidence.text: Note 8 of the Q2 FY26 10-Q states that [THE COMPANY] performed its review of the majority of its casualty insurance programmes during Q2 2026 and 'it was determined that there was no adjustment required for our total reserves related to prior years during the six months ended April 30, 2026' - so the item that produced a $(22.2)m pre-tax hit (~100bp of adjusted EBITDA margin, ~$0.26/sh) in Q4 FY25 is a Q2/Q4 event and is very unlikely to appear in the Q3 print, even though [THE COMPANY]'s adjusted EPS definition now includes it while its guidance range is stated 'before any impact from prior-year self-insurance adjustments'.
evidence.why_not_priced: [THE COMPANY] changed its non-GAAP definition after SEC staff comment (disclosed 2025-12-17) so that reported adjusted EPS now INCLUDES prior-year self-insurance adjustments, while the $3.85-$4.15 guide explicitly excludes them. That mismatch is the mechanical reason FY25 landed at $3.44 against a $3.65-$3.80 range, and it is the most plausible single source of a headline 'miss' on this name. Three analysts on a $2.8bn company are not reading Note 8 of a June 10-Q to work out the actuarial cadence, and there is no aggregator field for 'timing of casualty reserve reviews'. If the market had priced the absence of this risk you would not see an indicative 8.13% implied move on a 93-contract chain with a 1.32 put/call OI ratio. This is a left-tail-removal finding, not a mean finding, which is why it is [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: The $(22.2)m Q4 FY25 magnitude and the non-GAAP definition change come from a different document - the FY25 results release, [url removed] (2025-12-17). No other finding in this file rests on the 10-Q, so there is no source-cluster overlap.

evidence.text: [THE COMPANY]'s entire revenue growth story is one line: technical service income went RMB1.8m (Q4 2024) to RMB9.4m (Q1 2025) to RMB639.6m (Q4 2025) to RMB421.0m (Q1 2026) -- so it already fell 34.2% sequentially in Q1 2026 -- while brokerage income, the actual insurance business, was RMB648.6m / RMB670.8m / RMB724.8m over the same span, i.e. +11.7% YoY against the +64.8% headline, with sales and marketing rising from 22.9% to 43.6% of revenue and net profit falling to RMB98.4m from RMB108.2m.
evidence.why_not_priced: The decomposition requires subtracting the disclosed technical service line out of 'insurance-related income' -- a subtraction no aggregator performs, because every wire, Chinese and English, reprints the two headline numbers (+64.8% revenue, +74.1% insurance-related income) and stops. If the market had done the arithmetic, the last print on 2026-06-17 would not have paid +2.34% for a quarter in which net profit fell 9.1% YoY and the sole growth engine turned down 34% QoQ; there would be a published EPS consensus (there is none), and the only sell-side note on the tape would not be a UOB Kay Hian buy at US$2.20 dated 2025-03-14 ([url removed] eighteen months stale and citing FY2024 net profit growth of 119.8%. The company has never disclosed the composition or counterparties of the line; its stated definition includes 'marketing services to insurance companies, insurance brokers, and agency companies', i.e. a gross-up of resold traffic, which is exactly why S&M rose 213.8% for 5.3% more operating profit.
evidence.independence: Two separate Chinese outlets reached the same conclusion from the same disclosure without the QoQ inflection: Sina Finance, 2026-03-27, flagged the 354x jump to RMB639.6m and that it is 48.82% of insurance-related income with the composition and buyers undisclosed ([url removed] and Tencent News, 2026-04-11, argued the company 'spends more than one yuan to generate one yuan in revenue growth' ([url removed] The Q4 2025 RMB639.6m and the S&M/operating-profit series are cross-checked against the company's own Q4 exhibit ([url removed] and the Q2 2025 release, whose RMB97.3m operating profit matches my FY-minus-quarters derivation exactly. Note this finding and the Huize finding below point the same direction but rest on different documents and different mechanisms.

evidence.text: Huize Holding, the closest listed Chinese online life/health insurance brokerage, reported H1 2026 on 2026-08-20 with gross written premium +29.8% and first-year premium +48.7% but operating revenue up only 5.8% -- revenue per unit of premium fell from 21.1% to 17.2%, an 18.5% relative collapse in the channel take rate, in exactly the April-June window [THE COMPANY] is about to report.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a different ticker's release, published on 2026-08-20 -- after [THE COMPANY] last spoke about its business (2026-06-16) and before the 2026-08-25 date announcement -- and the coverage of it (TipRanks: 'Record Premiums and Profit Surge') read the premium and profit headlines, not the revenue-to-premium ratio. Nothing connects it to [THE COMPANY]: there is no shared analyst, no sector note, and [THE COMPANY]'s 20d run-up is +2.0%, i.e. the tape did not move on 2026-08-20. If the read-through were priced, [THE COMPANY] would have traded down that week rather than sitting pinned at $0.99-$1.00.
evidence.independence: [THE COMPANY]'s own numbers point the same way from a different document: brokerage income of RMB724.8m in Q1 2026 on FYP that grew 80.2% YoY as of Q2 2025 implies the same take-rate compression ([url removed] Directionally overlapping with finding 1 -- treat as partially redundant, which is why it is [sizing note removed].

evidence.text: [THE COMPANY] will report Q2 2026 with no CFO (vacant since Kangping Shi left in June 2022), no head of finance (Xiaoying Xu resigned as VP of finance and head of finance effective 2026-07-31), and a replacement audit-committee financial expert who took the seat only on 2026-07-01 after Heping Feng resigned from the audit, compensation and nominating committees -- two finance-governance exits inside 30 days, both immediately after the FY2025 20-F carrying the undisclosed RMB639.6m revenue line.
evidence.why_not_priced: The two events were reported separately and framed positively or neutrally by the only outlets that touched them: the director change was written up as '[THE COMPANY] Names New Independent Director and Audit Chair as Board Reshuffles' (TipRanks) and the finance exit as an AI-investment question by Simply Wall St ([url removed] Nobody has put the two 6-Ks next to each other, or next to the fact that the top finance job has been unfilled for four years. If the cluster were priced, the 2026-07-24 session would carry a volume spike -- it does not; the stock closed $1.12 that day, mid-range, and drifted.
evidence.independence: The second, separate 6-K: [url removed] dated 2026-06-23, which discloses Feng's resignation from all three board committees and Chang's appointment effective 2026-07-01. Feng's designation as the audit committee financial expert is stated in the FY2025 20-F ([url removed] Different filings, different dates, one theme -- I file it as one finding, not two.

evidence.text: The US$50 million share repurchase authorisation expires on 2026-09-09 -- the day after this print -- with the great majority unused (cumulative buybacks moved only from US$118.1m to US$120.1m between the Q4 and Q1 releases, and the 20-F puts usage under the September 2025 programme at US$9.5m as of 2026-03-31), and [THE COMPANY] has launched a new programme in September 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 and declared a US$0.03/ADS cash dividend alongside both its Q2 2025 and Q4 2025 results.
evidence.why_not_priced: The expiry date lives in one sentence of a twelve-month-old press release and appears in no calendar, no aggregator and no options market -- there is no options market on this name at all, so there is no mechanism by which a known forward event gets discounted here. A fresh authorisation of up to US$50m is roughly 11-14% of the US$366m market cap and about 190 sessions of the 254,685-ADS average volume, on a stock whose US$417.6m cash position exceeds its market cap. If this were priced, the run-in would not be +2.7% over five days off a 52-week low; a name with a near-certain buyback renewal and a ~6% annualised declared dividend yield would not be pinned at $0.99. The low end of my range is negative because the board has a live reason to skip the dividend this time: US$0.03 is 2.9% of a $1.02 spot and the ex-date would mechanically push the price under $1.00, so a dividend the holder base has come to expect could instead be cut or deferred.
evidence.independence: The five-programme history is stated in a different company document, the Q3 2025 release ([url removed] 2025-12-03): 'Pursuant to the share repurchase programs launched in September 2021, September 2022, September 2023, September 2024, and September 2025'. Cumulative-spend figures come from the Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 exhibits. This finding and the NYSE finding below both bear on the same announcement decision -- collapse them if scoring by cluster.

evidence.text: [THE COMPANY]'s NYSE Rule 802.01C 30-trading-day average closing price is $1.0263 as of 2026-09-04 (window 2026-07-27 to 2026-09-04), and the five sessions rolling out of that window closed $1.15/$1.15/$1.15/$1.14/$1.12, so the next five closes must average at least $0.984 to keep the average above $1.00 -- roughly 3.5% of cushion from the $1.02 spot, with the print the only scheduled catalyst inside that window.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a computation, not a disclosure: it requires taking 30 daily closes and averaging them, and no company release, no aggregator field and no wire story states it. The eye-catching detail in the same series is that [THE COMPANY] closed at exactly $1.00 for thirteen consecutive sessions (2026-08-05 to 2026-08-21) and exactly $0.99 for the six after -- a pin, not a random walk, on a $260k/day notional. If the threshold were priced, the run-in would show either accelerating decline or a squeeze, not nineteen sessions of a flat line inside a one-cent band; and there would be an English-language story on it, of which there are none. Signed slightly negative because a $1.02 stock five sessions from a non-compliance notice has a fatter left tail on a bad print -- mandates that cannot hold non-compliant names sell -- while the offsetting 'management acts to support the price' channel is already carried in the buyback finding above.
evidence.independence: Two Chinese outlets flag the threshold without doing the arithmetic: China Financial Online, 2026-08-06, '[THE COMPANY]'s share price touches the warning line' ([url removed] and a China Business Herald report of 2026-07-25 cited there on overseas-listed insurtechs falling below the US$1 line. Shares direction with, but is arithmetically independent of, the buyback finding; the price series is a different source from any company filing.

evidence.text: The sweep's lead hypothesis -- an NFRA commission-cap or 'reporting and execution consistency' (bao xing he yi) enforcement action landing in the April-June 2026 quarter -- does not hold. The non-auto bao xing he yi regime took effect 2025-11-01 ([url removed] and the regulator's unifying Q&A of January 2026 explicitly exempts short-term accident and health insurance, which is [THE COMPANY]'s fastest-growing FYP category ([url removed] The one Q2-adjacent requirement, real-time settlement for high-frequency internet-scenario business, starts 2026-07-01, i.e. Q3 not Q2. No Q2 regulatory shock; if anything the exemption is why [THE COMPANY] could push volume so hard.

An administrative penalty against the brokerage entity (Baoduoduo / [THE COMPANY] Insurance Brokerage) in 2026 -- searched the NFRA and PBoC penalty disclosure lists and Chinese financial press; found nothing naming the subsidiary.

An apparent RMB368m fall in the stated cash position between 2025-12-31 and 2026-03-31 looked like a cash burn against reported profit, but restricted cash rose RMB287m over the same balance sheet and total liabilities rose RMB588m, so it is premium float moving between line items, not burn. Dropped rather than filed.
A pending ADS ratio change or reverse split -- no announcement, no 6-K, nothing on the IR site.

First-year premium (FYP) for Q1 2026 -- the company disclosed FYP in the Q2 2025 release (RMB3,204.3m, +80.2%) but stopped giving a group FYP figure in the Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 releases, so the operating-cost-to-FYP ratio the sweep wanted cannot be computed for the current quarter. The omission itself is suggestive but I could not source it to anything beyond the absence.
Huimin / E-Find digital clinical trials as a swing factor -- it is RMB24.2m of RMB1,242.2m revenue growing 5.4% YoY; too small to move a print however it lands.

Any Form 4 or insider transaction cluster (foreign private issuer, so no Section 16 filings exist), and any current sell-side estimate revision on the name -- the newest broker note I could date is 2025-03-14.

evidence.text: [THE COMPANY]'s own narrowed FY26 guide implies Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $156-176mm, but the company itself quantified the prior-year Q4 as depressed by $40-50mm of cyber-incident adjusted EBITDA, so on a cyber-clean basis Q4 FY26 EBITDA is roughly flat to +13% (mid ~+3%) against reported growth of +34% to +52%, and against +23.4% in Q2 and +16.6% in Q3 — the underlying run-rate that has to support a ~$745-760mm FY27 guide on the way to the $800mm FY28 Investor Day target has decelerated to near zero.
evidence.why_not_priced: The arithmetic requires stitching three documents together: 39-week actuals (26-week adj EBITDA $346mm from the 2026-03-10 8-K plus $183mm Q3 from the 2026-06-09 8-K = $529mm), the narrowed FY26 guide of $685-705mm, and the July 2025 8-K's $40-50mm cyber EBITDA quantification. If the market had done it, the published Q4 consensus would not be sitting exactly on the guide midpoint (rev $7.705bn vs guide-implied $7.590-7.790bn; EPS $0.612 vs guide-implied $0.45-0.65, i.e. the 81st percentile of the company's own range) — consensus is modelling the reported optic, not the clean run-rate, and there is no visible FY27 whisper on a name the aggregators show with 2 estimates.
evidence.independence: Same-document cluster warning: the 39-week actuals and the guide come from [THE COMPANY]'s Q2/Q3 8-Ks, and the cyber quantification from the July 2025 8-K, so this is one arithmetic chain, not three findings. It shares its conclusion (FY27 guide risk) with the new-CFO finding below and the two should be read as overlapping. Independent corroboration of the FY28 anchor it is measured against: [url removed] (Investor Day, 2025-12-10, ~$33bn sales / ~$800mm adjusted EBITDA / ~$300mm FCF by FY28).

evidence.text: SNAP enrollment fell from 42.2 million in May 2025 to 36.6 million in May 2026 (-13%, faster than CBO projected, with Arizona -55%, Florida -22%), and this data was published on 2026-08-21 — after [THE COMPANY] last guided on 2026-06-09; [THE COMPANY]'s Conventional ($3.136bn) plus Retail ($515mm) segments were ~47% of Q3 FY26 net sales and are precisely the SNAP-exposed channels.
evidence.why_not_priced: [THE COMPANY] is modelled as a natural/organic growth story, not a SNAP name — its Q3 narrative and the sell-side framing are Natural segment growth and network optimisation, and management has never quantified SNAP exposure on a call. If this were priced into [THE COMPANY] specifically you would see Conventional-segment estimates cut and the FY27 sales bridge debated; instead [THE COMPANY] reiterated its FY26 midpoints on 2026-06-09 and the coverage that followed argued about the revenue miss, not the channel. The SNAP theme is priced into Kroger/Dollar General; it is not priced into the wholesaler two steps upstream.
evidence.independence: Circana estimates total SNAP EBT will fall ~$10bn in 2026 versus 2025, a separate commercial estimate from a separate publisher: [url removed] (2026-08-21).

evidence.text: Both listed natural-channel retailers reported negative traffic inside [THE COMPANY]'s Q4 window (2026-05-03 to 2026-08-01): Natural Grocers' quarter ended 2026-06-30 showed daily-average comps +1.2% built entirely on a +3.1% basket with transaction count -1.8% and gross margin down 60bp, and Sprouts' June quarter showed comps -1% with management citing weaker June trends — while [THE COMPANY]'s Natural segment (+4.4% in Q3) is the only growing part of the company and the pillar of the FY27 return-to-growth guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody carries [THE COMPANY] and NGVC in the same model — NGVC is a $335mm-a-quarter retailer and [THE COMPANY] is a $31bn wholesaler, and the read-through runs the wrong way for a screener. If the market had made this link, the negative-unit-volume debate would be in the [THE COMPANY] previews (which instead lead on the easy cyber comp and the +$0.62-vs-$(0.11) EPS optic) and [THE COMPANY]'s Natural-segment growth estimate would have been cut after 2026-08-06. NGVC itself fell 14% on the print, so the channel datapoint moved a price — just not this one.
evidence.independence: Sprouts Farmers Market's June-quarter comp of -1% with explicit weaker-June commentary is a second, larger, independently sourced natural-channel datapoint: [url removed] . Cuts the other way, and I am counting it: Amazon's physical-stores line held +4% over the same window (see next finding).

evidence.text: Amazon's physical-stores net sales — the reported line for Whole Foods, [THE COMPANY]'s largest customer at roughly a quarter of net sales — were $5,794mm in the June-2026 quarter versus $5,595mm a year earlier, +4% and +4% excluding FX, essentially unchanged from the +4.6% March-quarter pace, covering two-thirds of [THE COMPANY]'s Q4.

Its bigger use is as a read on management intent: with ~$632M of cash and investments post-transaction, $167M left on the $200M share authorisation as of 2026-03-31, and both its equity and its own bonds trading distressed, a fresh or upsized capital-return announcement alongside the print is a live positive tail that no preview I found flags. If this were priced, previews would be discussing GAAP-vs-adjusted for Q2 and the buyback runway rather than only the -25/-30% revenue guide.
evidence.independence: https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/oddity-tech-to-repurchase-50-million-of-exchangeable-notes-at-discount -- confirms the same transaction from a non-EDGAR source, which is also the evidence that coverage was thin. evidence.text: The US$10m buyback that drove the stock +21.5% on 2026-09-03 and anchored the +76% five-session run is 17 Education's sixth consecutive annual US$10m authorisation (Nov 2021, Sep 2022, Sep 2023, Sep 2024, Sep 2025, Sep 2026) and is a straight rollover of the identical US$10m program that ran 2025-09-04 to 2026-09-04 and expired four days before this one started.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 2026-09-03 release makes no reference to any prior program, and the identical predecessor was buried inside the 2025-09-04 Q2 earnings 6-K rather than issued as its own headline. Volume on 2026-09-03 was 2,789,500 ADS against a 20-day median of 4,600 before the event - a ~600x spike in a 10.86m-ADS name with no sell-side coverage and no option chain. If the market had recognised this as an expiring-program rollover rather than new capital, the tape would show a low-volume drift, not a 600x-volume +21.5% day followed by three more up sessions on no news at all; and the stock would not still be adding +18% intraday on 2026-09-08 on roughly average volume with nothing in the wire since 2026-09-03.
evidence.independence: Independent primary confirmation of the recurrence pattern from four separate filings, none of which is the 2026 release: the 2023-09-21 6-K authorising US$10m from 2023-11-02 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000095017023049313/yq-6k-09-22-2023.htm), the 2022-09-29 6-K authorising US$10m from 2022-11-02 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312522254314/d300245d6k.htm), the 2021-11-02 announcement of US$10m (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2021/11/02/2325327/0/en/17-Education-Technology-Group-Inc-Announces-US-10-Million-Share-Repurchase-Program-and-Plan-to-Implement-ADS-Ratio-Change.html), and the 2025-09-04 Q2 2025 release carrying the immediately-preceding US$10m authorisation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000095017025112952/yq-ex99_1.htm). The FY2025 20-F's XBRL tagging separately names ShareRepurchaseProgramInSeptemberTwoThousandAndTwentyFourMember and ...TwentyFiveMember (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821468/000119312526191472/yq-20251231.htm).

evidence.text: Q1 2026's headline RMB99.5m revenue (+359% YoY) was drawn largely out of a one-off pre-sale balance rather than new demand: deferred revenue and advances from customers fell from RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 to RMB104.5m at 2026-03-31, a RMB61.5m drawdown equal to 62% of the quarter's revenue, and cash plus term deposits fell RMB54.6m (RMB406.9m to RMB352.3m) against a reported net loss of only RMB19.4m - 2.8x the loss.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no sell-side model on a US$37.4m-market-cap name, no consensus estimate published, and every piece of wire copy on the quarter carried only the two lines the company led with - '+359.0% year-over-year' and 'Yiqi Aixue revenue more than quadrupled'. The Q1 earnings call had no Q&A at all (the operator recorded no questions), so the drawdown was never put to management. Had the market modelled the unwind, a stock at 0.73x its own liquid assets would not need a recurring buyback authorisation to re-rate 76%; the re-rating is being justified by the growth narrative, which is precisely the thing the deferred-revenue line qualifies. The remaining RMB104.5m balance also caps how much of this can repeat.
evidence.independence: The year-ago control comes from a DIFFERENT filing and shows the drawdown is not seasonal: in Q1 2025 deferred revenue fell only RMB40.4m to RMB36.9m, i.e. RMB3.5m or 16% of that quarter's RMB21.7m revenue, versus 62% this year, and cash plus deposits fell RMB25.9m against a LARGER net loss of RMB30.9m - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000095017025084635/yq-ex99_1.htm (2025-06-11). The Q4/FY2025 release shows where the balance came from - RMB40.4m at 2024-12-31 and RMB36.5m at 2025-09-30 building to RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 on pre-sales of the new consumer product: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526122709/yq-ex99_1.htm (2026-03-25) and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312525313418/yq-ex99_1.htm (2025-12-10). NOTE: the RMB61.5m deferred-revenue drawdown and the RMB54.6m cash decline are two readings of the same Q1 2026 document and are filed here as one finding, not two.

evidence.text: The company dismissed Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu as its auditor effective 2026-05-27 and appointed Marcum Asia CPAs LLP for the year ending 2026-12-31 - i.e. it dropped a Big Four auditor two quarters after its revenue recognition profile changed beyond recognition, and the Q2 2026 numbers about to be released are the first reported under the new firm.
evidence.why_not_priced: It was disclosed in a 6-K with no press release and no GlobeNewswire distribution - it does not appear in the company's news feed alongside the buyback, the earnings date or the Q1 results, and the stock's reaction that day was -4.0%. It is a dismissal initiated by the company, not a resignation, with no disagreements or reportable events cited, so there is no headline to attach it to. If the market had weighted it, a name that just re-rated 76% on a boilerplate buyback would not be paying up for the same audited growth story; the coverage would carry a governance qualifier and it carries none.
evidence.independence: Points the same way as, but is documented separately from, the revenue-quality finding above (different filing, different date, different subject matter). No third-party source independently flags it - no analyst, ratings agency or short report on this name was found.

evidence.text: Buyback fundability/capacity: the 'is the US$10m actually payable offshore' angle is dead. The FY2025 20-F condensing schedule shows Cayman-plus-other-subsidiary cash of RMB34.5m and term deposits of RMB160.5m - roughly US$27m of offshore liquidity against a US$10m authorisation, so capacity is not the constraint. The constraint is willingness, which is what finding 1 is about.

Insider-buying cluster: the 13 Form 4s between 2026-07-06 and 2026-09-04 look like a CEO accumulating into the print, but today's 13D/A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526384376/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml, 2026-09-08) discloses them as 110,628 ADS for ~US$0.24m total bought 2026-06-30 to 2026-09-03 under a Rule 10b5-1 plan running to 2028-03-31. Automated, pre-committed, ~US$24k a clip, and therefore carries zero information about the quarter. This is a lead that dies on inspection.

Going-private / take-private setup: Andy Chang Liu holds 41.30% of shares and 95.0% of votes and the company trades below net cash, but the 13D/A of 2026-09-08 states the purchases are 'for investment purposes' with no mention of a merger, tender offer or going-private proposal.

Nasdaq listing deficiency: no minimum bid price, market-value-of-publicly-held-shares or ADS-ratio notice found in the FY2025 20-F or anywhere in the 2026 filing stream. Last ADS ratio change was 2021 (to 1 ADS : 10 Class A, now 1:50); nothing pending.

Any news at all in the window that would justify the 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-08 second leg (+18% intraday on 2026-09-08 on roughly average volume): the company news feed is empty between 2026-09-03 and the print. Checked stocktitan, GlobeNewswire, Yahoo press releases, EDGAR.

Consumer footprint for Yiqi Aixue, the product carrying the entire growth story: no App Store or Google Play listing findable under that exact name, no appearance in any of the 2026 618 or summer Chinese learning-device buying guides (which list 作业帮, 小猿, 学而思, 科大讯飞, 步步高), and no ranking or download data on Qimai reachable. Treated as unsourced absence and NOT filed as a finding - Chinese app and e-commerce data are poorly indexed from here and an absence in US search is not evidence.

Paying-user, subscription or hardware-unit metrics: the company has never disclosed one. Not in the Q1 2026 release, not in the Q1 call (which had no Q&A), not in the Chinese-language Q1 PR. So there is no user metric to trend into this print.

Q2 2026 guidance: none exists. The only forward statement on the Q1 call was qualitative - 'strong year-over-year revenue growth and continued improvement in operating performance throughout 2026' with an explicit warning that 'quarterly results may vary'. There is no number for the print to beat or miss.
Government/school tender awards for the To-G and To-B smart-education lines: not retrievable from here; Chinese public procurement portals were not reachable through the available tooling.

Deferred revenue and advances from customers fell from RMB165.9m at 31-Dec-2025 to RMB104.5m at 31-Mar-2026, so RMB61.4m of the RMB99.5m of Q1 revenue that produced the headline '+359% YoY' was a drawdown of Q4 2025 pre-sale orders: implied new billings were only about RMB38m, less than the RMB43.2m spent on sales and marketing in the same quarter, and cash plus restricted cash plus term deposits fell RMB54.6m (RMB407.0m to RMB352.4m) against a reported net loss of just RMB19.4m.
evidence.why_not_priced: The wire copy on this quarter is 'AI learning app lifts 17EdTech revenue 359%, net loss down 37.4%' — headline growth and headline loss. The deferred-revenue line sits in the condensed balance sheet at the back of the same release and nobody has subtracted it: no sell-side analyst publishes an estimate on YQ, stockanalysis.com's news feed carries only the three headline items, and the release contains no cash-flow statement so the RMB54.6m cash decline versus a RMB19.4m loss has to be computed by differencing two balance sheets. If this were priced, the stock would not have closed the entire discount to book — shareholders' equity of RMB269.1m (US$39.0m) at 31-Mar-2026 against a US$37.5m market cap at $3.45 puts YQ at roughly 1.0x a book value that is falling about RMB18m a quarter, i.e. the deep-value cushion that justified the whole run has already gone. With only RMB104.5m of deferred balance left, the Q2 release's own deferred-revenue and cash lines are where this becomes visible for a second consecutive quarter.
evidence.independence: Chinese trade coverage independently describes the Q4 2025 launch as a membership product sold on pre-orders ('achieved strong pre-sale orders'), which is the mechanism: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526122709/yq-ex99_1.htm (2026-03-25). Separately, Tencent News coverage of 2026-07-12 attributes the growth to a To-B/To-G 'smart paper-pen + AI' school solution covering 2,000+ schools rather than to the consumer app the English release credits, which is a second, unrelated reason to doubt the revenue narrative: https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260712A066GD00. Note the RMB61.4m, RMB38m and RMB54.6m figures all come from the single Q1 6-K exhibit and are one finding, not three.

evidence.text: The US$10 million buyback authorisation announced 2026-09-03 that triggered the +21.5% jump is at least the fourth identical US$10 million 12-month authorisation the company has issued (November 2021, September 2024, September 2025, September 2026), and the FY2024 20-F discloses that only approximately US$0.1 million had actually been repurchased under the September 2024 programme as of 31-Dec-2024 — about 1% of the authorisation.
evidence.why_not_priced: Volume on the announcement day was 2,789,500 ADSs against a 20-day pre-event median of 4,600 — a 600x spike. That is a buyer base that arrived on the headline, not one that pulled the 2024 20-F. If the recycling were priced, the third and fourth iterations of an identical press release would have produced no move at all, and the aggregator write-ups would say 'renews' rather than 'Approves $10M Share Buyback' and 'announces NEW share repurchase program'. The company also has RMB104.5m of deferred revenue and a RMB54.6m quarterly cash decline standing in front of the RMB71m the authorisation would cost, which is a capacity constraint the 2024 execution rate already demonstrated.
evidence.independence: The prior identical authorisations are documented in three separate places: the 2021 release at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2021/11/02/2325327/0/en/17-Education-Technology-Group-Inc-Announces-US-10-Million-Share-Repurchase-Program-and-Plan-to-Implement-ADS-Ratio-Change.html (URL path confirms 2021, not 2026), the FY2024 20-F which contains the phrase 'repurchased approximately US$0.1 million' (single hit for this CIK on EDGAR full-text search) at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000095017025058824/yq-20241231.htm, and the FY2025 20-F whose inline-XBRL tags include 'ShareRepurchaseProgramInSeptemberTwoThousandAndTwentyFive' at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526191472/yq-20251231.htm.

evidence.text: The CEO's near-daily Form 4 open-market ADS purchases through August and early September — reported by aggregators as conviction buying — are executions of a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan entered into on 2026-03-31 with Tiger Brokers (NZ) Limited covering 30-Jun-2026 to 31-Mar-2028, a fact disclosed for the first time in Item 6 of a Schedule 13D/A filed on the morning of the print itself.
evidence.why_not_priced: The plan was signed on 31-Mar-2026, before Q2 even began, so the purchases carry zero information about the quarter being reported — yet the coverage that exists reads the opposite way: 'Chang Liu Purchases 10,000 Shares of 17 Education & Technology Group' framed as insider conviction, on a site that even gets the exchange wrong (NYSE:YQ; YQ is Nasdaq). The 13D/A was filed hours before the release, has no wire pickup, and its only exhibit is a boilerplate joint filing agreement with no economics in it — so if the market had read it, today's roughly +18% would not be happening on a day whose sole company document adds nothing. The purchases are also tiny in dollars: 10,000 ADSs at $2.3788 is $23,800, and the transactions coded 'L' are Rule 16a-6 small acquisitions of 2 to 1,857 ADSs.
evidence.independence: The Form 4s themselves, filed by a different route, show the mechanical daily cadence and the trivial size: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821468/000119312526341197/ownership.xml (filed 2026-08-10, transactions 3-6 Aug at $2.11-$2.16) and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526382783/ownership.xml (filed 2026-09-04, 10,000 ADS at $2.3788). The misreading in third-party coverage is at https://www.thecerbatgem.com/2026/09/04/chang-liu-purchases-10000-shares-of-17-education-technology-group-nyseyq-stock.html. Shares its source document with the +2.0 structural-bid finding below.

evidence.text: Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu was dismissed as auditor effective 2026-05-27 — four weeks after signing the FY2025 20-F and three weeks before the Q1 revenue inflection was reported — and replaced by Marcum Asia CPAs LLP, a firm the PCAOB censured and fined US$100,000 on 2025-09-23.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 6-K disclosing the change moved the stock -3.99% on 4,600-share median volume — that is not a market clearing an information event, that is a filing nobody read. There is no analyst coverage to write it up, the change was reported as a dismissal with no disagreements and no reportable events so it generated no wire story, and it has never been connected in print to the fact that the revenue line inflected 359% in the very quarter that straddles the change. If it were priced, a Big-Four-to-second-tier downgrade at a China ADR carrying a large deferred-revenue balance would show as a persistent governance discount rather than a 1.0x book multiple after a 76% run. Q2 is the first release published under the new engagement.
evidence.independence: PCAOB's own sanction release, an entirely separate source: https://pcaobus.org/news-events/news-releases/news-release-detail/pcaob-sanctions-u.s.-audit-firm-for-violations-related-to-communications-between-predecessor-and-successor-auditors (2025-09-23). A same-quarter CFO change points the same way — Sishi Zhou was confirmed as CFO on 2026-03-24 after nine months as Acting CFO: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526120598/yq-ex99_1.htm.

evidence.text: There is a real structural bid under the stock that cuts against the fade: the CEO's 10b5-1 plan runs to 31-Mar-2028 and the US$10m authorisation is live, against a non-Liu share base of only about 6.4m ADS-equivalent (542.2m shares outstanding less Andy Chang Liu's 223.9m / 41.30%) and a pre-spike median volume of 4,600 ADSs a day.
evidence.why_not_priced: The float arithmetic requires combining the 13D/A percentages with the 20-F share count, and no aggregator does it: stockanalysis.com reports 10.86m shares outstanding and a US$37.45m market cap with no float adjustment at all. A stock where 41.3% is held by one person and baseline turnover is 4,600 ADSs a day cannot absorb even partial execution of a US$10m programme without gapping, so the downside from the four negative findings above is genuinely dampened relative to what the fundamentals alone would imply — which is why my net number is -9.5 and not the -11.5 the negatives sum to.
evidence.independence: Share count from the FY2025 20-F cover: 'As of December 31, 2025, there were 542,229,838 ordinary shares outstanding' — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526191472/yq-20251231.htm (2026-04-29). Market cap and 10.86m ADS from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/yq/ (2026-09-08). Shares its source document with the 10b5-1 finding above and is the opposite-signed reading of it.

evidence.text: [THE COMPANY]'s Q2 FY27 revenue guide of $219-221m is flat sequentially on Q1's $220m, but the company's only observable prior year grew +9.6% sequentially over the same fiscal quarters (Q1 FY26 $157.1m -> Q2 FY26 $172.2m, derivable from the disclosed 9M FY26 revenue of $524.3m less Q3 FY26 of $195m, and cross-checked by the stated 40% and 28% YoY growth rates); consensus of $220.5m is the guide midpoint to within $0.5m, so the street has not applied that seasonality at all.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the street had modelled last year's shape it would carry ~$230-241m for Q2, not $220.5m. Consensus landing inside the guide band by half a million dollars is the visible fingerprint of guide-anchoring on a company with only four public quarters and no consensus seasonality template. Had it been priced, the option-implied move would not need to be 14% and the 25d skew would not be +5.64 vol points paid for downside into a print the sell-side has raised targets into three times in three weeks.
evidence.independence: The Q2 revenue guide and the Q1 FY27 base come from a different document, the 2026-06-10 8-K exhibit [url removed] ; the $220.5m consensus figure comes from a third source, Oppenheimer's 2026-08-27 preview at [url removed]

evidence.text: The price half of [THE COMPANY]'s gross bookings accelerated sharply across its fiscal Q2 (May-Jul 2026): US CPI airline fares ran +26.7%, +26.5% and +25.5% YoY in May/Jun/Jul against +7.1%, +14.9% and +20.7% in Feb/Mar/Apr, its fiscal Q1 -- roughly a 12pp step-up -- while consensus gross bookings of $2.86bn implies a 7.7% sequential DECLINE from Q1's $3.1bn, versus a roughly +1% sequential move in the same fiscal quarters a year earlier.
evidence.why_not_priced: Gross bookings is [THE COMPANY]'s headline KPI and it is a dollar figure, so it mechanically inherits fare inflation; nobody maps the BLS air-fare series onto a fiscal quarter that runs May-July. If it were priced, previews would frame the quarter on booking VALUE rather than on client wins and AI engagement, and consensus bookings growth would not be set 13pp below the prior quarter's realised 50% exactly as the price input doubled. evidence.text: [THE COMPANY]'s Q1 10-Q states it has filed IEEPA tariff refund claims and will 'recognize any related refunds and interest when cash is received' — and CBP's own refund machinery (CAPE Phase I opened 2026-04-20, disbursement target 45 days post-validation, 60-90 days from acceptance) puts that cash squarely inside the quarter being reported tomorrow, which ended 2026-08-01.

The magnitude anchor is management's own: the CFO said on the 2026-03-12 call that 'Tariffs increased year-end inventory value by approximately $4.2 million' against a $76m inventory balance, so the annual incremental-duty run-rate flowing through COGS is a multiple of that and a refund plus statutory interest of a few million dollars is ~$0.10-0.18 per share on 28.4m shares — enough to flip a guided loss quarter to reported profit, and ~25-40% of the company's $12.5m cash balance. If this were priced you would see the stock bid into the event rather than -11.64% over five sessions, you would see a preview note naming a one-time refund line (there is none — no wire item on [THE COMPANY] since the 2026-09-01 date announcement), and a $89m-cap name would not be carrying a single estimate.
